names.name: Acamar
names.origin: From its name for the Arabic Almagest period akhir al-nahr, "the River's End". Applied in medieval times, and reapplied in recent times

names.name: Achernar
names.origin: Arabic name (āhiru n-nahr) meaning, the End of the River; originally used for theta Eri that was considered the end of the river in the ancient star catalog (Almagest).The name was transferred to alpha Eri in the Early Modern Era when the constellation was extended south to this new terminus.

names.name: Achird
names.origin: The proper name Achird was apparently first applied to Eta Cassiopeiae in the Skalnate Pleso Atlas of the Heavens published in Slovacia in 1950, but is not known prior to that.

names.name: Acrab
names.origin: Arabic name al-'Aqrab for the constellation Scorpius ("the scorpion") (e.g. Al Sufi). Application of the transliteration "Acrab" specifically to the pair Beta1 and Beta2 Sco was made by Piazzi (1814) in the Palermo Catalog, and its use spread through the 19th century.

names.name: Acrux
names.origin: A modern creation (1938) that is derived from Bayer's nomenclature by combining the "A" from the "alpha" in alpha Crucis and the Latin constellation name in the nominative case.

names.name: Acubens
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from the Arabic word al-zubana, "the claw", used in Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos in describing the stars alpha and iota Cnc. Otherwise, the same Arabic word was used for the "claws" of Scorpius.

names.name: Adhafera
names.origin: From the name for the Arabic Almagest period al-dafira, "the Lock of Hair," for the Coma Berenices cluster. Wrongly applied to zeta Leonis in recent times. Yet, misapplications of terms for the "hairy" cluster that is called "Coma" to the mane of the lion can be traced back to (at least) the 17th century.

names.name: Adhara
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic asterism name al-'adhara, "the Virgins", for epsilon, delta, eta and omicron2 CMa. The significance of the name is unknown.

names.name: Adhil
names.origin: From the Arabic word al-dhail, "the hem of a robe or dress", used in the Arabic Almagest in describing 49 And and chi And, and transliterated in the Medieval Latin Almagest as adhil. This word was wrongly applied as a star name to xi And in recent times.

names.name: Aerostaticus
names.origin: Globus Aerostaticus is one of the obsolete constellations, introduced in early modern time to celebrate new technologies.

names.name: Ain
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the name for the Arabic Almagest period ain al-thaur "the Bull's Eye," for a Tau. Applied to epsilon Tau in recent times (Ptolemy had alpha Tau the southern eye, and epsilon Tau on the northern eye).

names.name: Ainalrami
names.origin: Arabic ain al-rāmī (simplified Ainalrami) means The Eye of the Archer. It originates from Arabic Almagest translations.

names.name: Aladfar
names.origin: Aladfar derives from the Arabic al- uzfur "the talons (of the swooping [eagle])" which designates and asterism consisting of mu and eta Lyr. It was made popular by Allen.

names.name: Alaybasan
names.origin: Al-Aybasān, the Two Joints (of bones), is an Indigenous Arabian asterism. Name variants are Al-Anīsān and Al-Baysan. The later spelling variant al-Anīsān that originated from a mistake changed the meaning, as it translates The Two Friends. WGSN adopts a spelling variant without hyphen: "Alaybasan" is the name for beta Tri

names.name: Albaldah
names.origin: The name of the 21st Arabic lunar station, Al-Baldah (The empty area), designates a starless region between zeta Sgr and alpha Cap; the star pi Sgr is at its northern edge and was wrongly attributed with this name by Allen (1899, 359).

names.name: Albali
names.origin: From the Arabic word bali("swallower", used in an Arabic discussion pertaining to the Arabic lunar mansion name sa(d bula((given for epsilon, mu and nu Aqr; of unknown meaning). In recent times the Arabic article al- was added to bali(and the word was applied as a star name.

names.name: Albireo
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with Ptolemy's name for the constellation Cygnus -, "the Bird". The Arabs transliterated this name as urnis. The Medieval Latin translator of the Arabic Almagest, in turn, did not recognize any Greek word behind urnis (or whatever Arabic corruption he may have read), so he merely transliterated it into a form which appeared int he manuscripts variously as eurisim, eirisun, eirism, etc. In a note appended to this Medieval Latin constellation name for Cygnus, one Latin commentator ventured to derive it from the name of an aromatic herb he knew: ireus. This erroneous commentary read, in brief part: "eirisim...ab ireo", or, "[the constellation name] eirisim...[coming] from [the word] ireus". Apparently in one manuscript of the Latin Almagest, the final word of this commentary, ab ireo, were written on the next line below the constellation title, where the descriptions of the stars begin. Since the first star entered in the Almagest under the constellation Cygnus is beta Cyg, the words ab ireo seem to have been confused as a name for this star. "Arabicized" with the insertion of the letter "l", ab ireo, written as "Albireo", was applied as a star name to beta Cyg by Early Modern times.

names.name: Alchiba
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name al-khibā, “the Tent,” for beta, gamma, delta and epsilon Crv. Wrongly applied as a star name to alpha Crv in recent times.

names.name: Alcor
names.origin: Ultimately from the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-jaun, for epsilon UMa, which was transliterated and eventually corrupted in Latin to "Alcor." The name was wrongly transferred to 80 UMa in Early Modern times.

names.name: Alcyone
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Aldebaran
names.origin: Applied in the early Islamic period from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-dabaran, possibly meaning "the Follower," alternatively used as the lunar mansion name for all the Hyades (or again for alpha Tau alone). The name is thought to refer to this star's following the Pleiades across the sky, or to the Hyades (or alpha Tau) coming after the Pleiades as a lunar mansion. "Aldebaran" is one of the oldest Arabic star names applied in the West, from the end of the 10th century A.D.

names.name: Alderamin
names.origin: Applied to alpha Cep since medieval times. The erroneous derivation understood since Early Modern times was from al-dhira (al)yamin, "the Right Forearm," an assumed Arabic descriptive term for alpha Cep. Firstly, in the Almagest, alpha Cep is described on the right "shoulder" (Arabic al-katif or al-mankib) of Cepheus, whereas no right "forearm" (al-dhira<) is described for the figure. Secondly, in Arabic, "right forearm" is spelled correctly as al-dhira al-yumna, which (in contrast to al-yamin) lacks assonance in the last syllable to Alderamin. Therefore, it is more likely that Alderamin is derived from the various medieval Christian abbreviations of muqaddam al-dhira<ain, "the Preceding One of the Two Cubits, or Forearms," which was a name for the Arabic Almagest period (based on pre-Islamic Arabian) for alpha Gem. This would have been wrongly transferred to alpha Cep in medieval times.

names.name: Aldhanab
names.origin: Al Dhanab from Arabic (adh-dhanab), The Tail, became common since its mentioning in Allen (1899). There it is attributed to a Persian astronomer but the whole constellation Grus is a constellation invented in the Early Modern Era.

names.name: Aldhibah
names.origin: zeta and eta Draconis together had been considered the asterism of, al-dhi b, Two Hyenas or Two Wolfs that are lurking for the Camel's Foal that is protected by its mother (other stars in Draco).

names.name: Aldulfin
names.origin: Arabic scholarship adopted the Greek loanword "dulfim" or "dulfin" (with article: ad-dulfin or simplified adulfin) for the marine mammal. The star epsilon Del at the dorsal fin of the Ptolemaic (smaller than ancient Greek) figure was called Al Dhanab al Dulfim (the Dolphin's Tail) and as there are many stars named with the Arabic root for "tail", WGSN adopted only the last part of the name.

names.name: Alfarasalkamil
names.origin: Alfarasalkamil means "The Complete Horse", as opposed to the Greek constellation of a half horse that is now called Pegasus. The Arabian tradition may perhaps root in or connect to the Babylonian one.

names.name: Alfirk
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian names kaukaba al-firq (for alpha and beta Cep), and kawakib al-firq (for alpha, beta, and eta Cep). kaukaba and kawakib mean "two stars" and "stars" (more than two), respectively, but the original Arabic script for al-firq can be vocalized in various ways with various meanings. If the vocalization al-firq is accepted, it means "the Flock," and may refer to a flock of sheep here.

names.name: Algedi
names.origin: Reapplied in recent times (from its older medieval spelling), from the scientific Arabic constellation name al-jady, "the Kid," for Capricornus.

names.name: Algenib
names.origin: From the name for the Arabic Almagest period al-janb, "the Side," for alpha Per. Wrongly transferred to gamma Peg in Early Modern times.

names.name: Algieba
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-jabha "the Forehead," for zeta, gamma, eta, and alpha Leo, associated with the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism al-asad.

names.name: Algol
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period ras al-ghul "the Demon's Head" (for Ptolemy's Gorgon-head). "Algol" is one of the oldest Arabic star names applied in the West, from the end of the 10th century A.D.

names.name: Algorab
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the name for the Arabic Almagest period janab al-ghurab, "the Raven's Wing," for gamma Crv. Transferred to delta Crv in Early Modern times (both gamma and delta were on the Raven's wings in the Almagest).

names.name: Alhena
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-bana, possibly meaning "the Mark on the Neck of a Camel," for gamma and xi Gem, or alternatively for gamma, xi, eta, mu, and v Gem.

names.name: Alioth
names.origin: Ultimately from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-jaun, "the Black Horse, or Bull," which became corrupted even in Arabic sources (where some of the corruptions carried other meanings). For example, in the Arabic manuscript of the Almagest that was translated into Latin in 1175 A.D., this name of epsilon UMa had apparently been miswritten as al-jauza or al-jauza (the latter being identical to the name for the Arabic Almagest period for Orion and Gemini). Whatever was read in this Arabic manuscript was transliterated into Latin as alioze. In subsequent Latin copies, this name was further corrupted to aliore, Alcor, Alioth, etc. Since late medieval times, "Alioth" became the preferred name for epsilon UMa.

names.name: Aljanah
names.origin: The star used to be commonly named Gienah (cf. Kunitzsch and Smart 2006, Allen 1899) which derives from Arabic al-Janāh, The Wing, based on Almagest translations. WGSN adopted the original Arabic word instead of the corrupted one.

names.name: Alkaid
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qa'id, "the Leader" (probably as leader of the Daughters of the Bier).

names.name: Alkalurops
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with one of the words used by Ptolemy to describe this star in the Almagest:, "club", rarely used as "sphepherd's staff". This word was transliterated into Arabic as qulurubus, and hence into Latin as calurus. Then in Early Modern times, the derivation of calurus was mistakenly attributed to another Greek word:, "shepherd's staff". This erroneous word, in its turn, was transliterated into Latin, then Arabicized with the article al-, then its spelling corrupted, to become "Alkalurops", which was thereafter applied as a star name to mu Boo.

names.name: Alkaphrah
names.origin: corrupted spelling of Arabic al-qafzah "the leap" of the Indigenous Arabic group of gazelle asterisms preserved in Ibn Qutaybah.

names.name: Alkarab
names.origin: traditional Arabic name Al Karab, The Bucket-rope, was an asterism consisting of tau and upsilon Peg

names.name: Alkes
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from the Arabic constellation name al-ka's, "the (Wine) Cup," for Crater.

names.name: Almaaz
names.origin: The Arabic term (al-ma az) can refer to the plural "goats" but has also been interpreted as a He-Goat (contrasting Capella, the She-Goat). Allen (1899, 90) cites Hyde's 1665 translation of Ulugh Beg with this term for a group of stars (asterism or sub-constellation) in Auriga.

names.name: Almach
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the Arabic name for this star: anaq al-ard, "the Caracal" (a black-eared feline predator found in the Middle East). The Arabs also gave the name in short form as al- anaq, which became transliterated into Medieval Latin as alamac. Later, the derivatin of alamac was erroneously attributed to the assumed Arabic word al-maq (properly al-muq) for "the boot" or "buskin", rather than to al- anaq. Subsequently the erroneous word, as "Almaak" and later "Almach" was applied as a star name to gamma And, mostly in astronomical works in English. Other, non-English works use the spelling "Alamak" derived directly from the Medieval Latin transliteration.

names.name: Almighzal
names.origin: Wool Spindle – central Saudi Arabia. The constellation is used in a contemporary oral tradition by the ordinary people.

names.name: Alnair
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its late Arabic name al-nayyir min dhanab al-but, "the Bright One from the Fish's Tail" (where a l6th century Arabic astronomer had extended Ptolemy's Southern Fish [Piscis Austrinus] into what is today Grus). The form Al Na'ir was taken from a wrong transliteration (Al Na'ir) of the Arabic adjective al-nayyir, "the Bright One."

names.name: Alnasl
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its late Arabic name al-nasl, "the Point," in turn an abbreviation of the Arabic Almagest's nasl al-sahm, "the Point of the Arrow."

names.name: Alnilam
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name al-nizam, "the String of Pearls," for delta, epsilon, and zeta Ori.

names.name: Alnitak
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name nitaq al-jauza, "the Belt (or Girdle) of al-jauza," for delta, epsilon, and zeta Ori.

names.name: Alniyat
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-niyat, "the Arteries", for sigma and tau Sco. alpha Sco, between the arteries, was the pre-Islamic Arabian qalb al'aqrab, "the Scorpion's Heart" (all were part of the pre-Islamic Arabian Scorpion).

names.name: Alphard
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-fard, "the Solitary One," descriptive of this star's standing out among the surrounding dim stars. (See the same word in the plural, with zeta CMa.)

names.name: Alphecca
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name al-fakka, for Corona Borealis. The Arabic name, from the root f-k-k, "to separate, break up, etc.," apparently refers to this asterism's shape: an incomplete circle.

names.name: Alpheratz
names.origin: The specific origin of this name is unclear. It may represent a transfer from beta Peg, where alferaz and other variants were applied in medieval times as abbreviations for beta Peg's Arabic name mankib al-faras, "the Horse's Shoulder". Or, it may be from an abbreviation of the name alpheraz id est equus, "alpheraz, that is, the Horse", which was applied directly to alpha And also in medieval times. In any case, Medieval Latin authors confused these two names, their spellings, and their identifications, and the modern application of "Alpheratz" to alpha And comes down to us from late medieval times.

names.name: Alqiladah
names.origin: al-Qilāda, “the necklace”, is an Indigenous Arabian six star asterism recorded by al Sūfī, Ibn Qutayba, and al Marzūqī.

names.name: Alqubba
names.origin: al-Qubba, “the dome or domed tent”, is an Arab asterism that correspond to the stars of Corona Australis.

names.name: Alrakis
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-raqis, "the Trotting Camel."

names.name: Alrescha
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-risha', "the Cord," for beta And. Wrongly transferred to alpha Psc in recent times. According to a Arabic source, the pre-Islamic Arabian al-risha' included, in a larger sense, two curving lines of mostly dim stars in Andromeda and Pisces, meant to attach to the pre-Islamic Arabian al-dalw "the Well Bucket" (marked by today's Square of Pegasus). It is also possible that this "cord" was a remnant of the cord joining the two fish of the older Babylonian zodiac. Indeed, these stars of the cord were alternatively known by the pre-Islamic Arabians as al-hut, "the Fish" (a single fish), corresponding to what in other cultures was Pisces among the zodiacal signs (and according to this tradition, the Fish's brightest star, beta And, was batn al-hut, "the Fish's Belly").

names.name: Alruba
names.origin: Arabic Al Ruba translates "the foal" and specifically refers to a young camel born in the spring. The name was considered traditional by WGSN in 2018 as it is listed in Allen (1899).

names.name: Alrumh
names.origin: Al-Rumh, the Lance/ Spear, is an Arabic asterism from pre-Islamic times that covers the area between Epsilon, Upsilon, Eta and Sigma Bootis. The named star is close to the dominant Epsilon Bootis, which also forms part of the Chinese constellation of The Lance (Genghe).

names.name: Alsafi
names.origin: Alsafi is corrupted from Athāfi, erroneously transcribed from the Arabic plural Athāfiyy, by which the nomads designated the tripods of their open-air kitchens; one of these being imagined in sigma, tau and upsilon [Dra].

names.name: Alsamaka
names.origin: Al-Samaka al-Suġrā (Arabic:, The Smaller Fish) is an Arabic asterism in Lacerta and Andromeda, attested since Ibn Qutayba.

names.name: Alsciaukat
names.origin: misspelled Arabic aš-šawkat (al-shaukat), The Thorn. The name obviously has nothing to do with the figure of the lynx (or historically sometimes called "Tiger" or "Tigris") that was invented in Early Modern Times.

names.name: Alsephina
names.origin: The term is Arabic for "The Ship". It originates from the translation of Greek knowledge to Arabic when Argo Navis (The Ship Argo) was translated to Arabic and, thus, originally referred to the whole constellation rather than any specific star.

names.name: Alshain
names.origin: Applied in recent times (with a misreading in the second word) from abbreviating the Persian asterism name shahin-i tarazu, "the Scale Beam," for alpha, beta and gamma Aql. The Persian name, in turn, was a medieval translation of these stars' pre-Islamic Arabian name al-mizan, "the Balance" (said to be a popular name for the pre-Islamic Arabians al-nasr al-ti'ir listed under alpha Aql).

names.name: Alshat
names.origin: The Arabic term, Sa d al-Dhābih, The Lucky Asterism of the Slaughterer (22 lunar station), consists of the 3 stars: alpha1, beta and nu Cap. As alpha and beta already have proper names, the corrupted form "shat" (for sad) was used to name nu Cap.

names.name: Altair
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from an abbreviation of its Arabic name al-nars al-ta)ir, "the Flying Eagle (or Vulture)", alternatively used as an asterism name for alpha, beta and gamma Aql. The name has probable origins among the Babylonians and Sumerians, for whom alpha Aql was "the Eagle Star".

names.name: Altais
names.origin: Applied in recent times from a misreading of the script for the Arabic constellation name al-tinnin, "the Serpent," as it appeared incorrectly in a late Arabic star catalog, as part of the name for delta Dra. (The incorrect word, al-tais, is a real word in Arabic meaning "the He-goat," however it was never used by the pre-Islamic Arabians in stellar nomenclature. Furthermore, in the same Arabic source, in the name of epsilon Dra [formed parallel to that of delta Dra], the word was correctly written al-tinnin.)

names.name: Alterf
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-tarf, "the Glance," for kappa Cnc and lambda Leo, associated with the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism al-asad, as if being located on that lion's eyes.

names.name: Aludra
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the alternative Arabic asterism name al-(udhra, "the Virginity", and (udhrat aljauza), "the Virginity [?] of al-jauza)", for epsilon, delta, eta and omicron2 CMa. The name (udhrat al-jauza), by tying it with the nearly Arabic asterism al-jauza) (today's Orion), may have been an attempt to apply significance to the enigmatic and perhaps older name al-(udhra.

names.name: Alula Australis
names.origin: Applied in recent times from their pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qafza al-ula, "the First Leap", and the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern," respectively.

names.name: Alula Borealis
names.origin: Applied in recent times from their pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qafza al-ula, "the First Leap", and the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern," respectively.

names.name: Alwasl
names.origin: al-Wasl, “the Joint" or "Connection” is an Arabic name for the sky region between "al-Na ām al-Wārid”, the incoming ostriches and "al-Na ām alSādir”, the outgoing ostriches.

names.name: Alya
names.origin: From the Arabic word alya, naming the fatty tail of a breed of Eastern sheep. In Early Modern times this word was erroneously proposed as the origin of Alioth, a Medieval Latin name for epsilon UMa. The erroneous "Alya" was applied as a star name to theta Ser in recent times.

names.name: Alzirr
names.origin: Arabic, al-zirr, "the button". Allen (1899) attributes the name to Al Birūnī and it certainly does not have Greek roots as it is located at the foot of the eastern Twin.

names.name: Ancha
names.origin: A Latin word meaning "hip", used in the Medieval Latin Almagest in describing sigma and iota/38 Aqr in the right and left hips, respectively (following an error, for Ptolemy had these stars in "the buttocks"). The word was applied as a star name to theta Aqr (correctly in Ptolemy's "right socket of the hip") in recent times.

names.name: Angetenar
names.origin: derived from the Arabic Al Hināyat an-Nahr, 'the Bend in the River', based on Arabic Almagest translations

names.name: Ankaa
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the modern Arabic constellation name al-'anqa' (a fabulous bird) for Phoenix.

names.name: Anser
names.origin: Johannes & Elisabetha Hevelius created “Vulpecula cum Ansere” (the Little Fox with the Goose) out of unformed stars in the space between Cygnus and Aquila. The constellation first appeared in Firmamentum Sobiescianum sive Uranographia (1687) and the accompanying introductory text, Prodromus astronomiae (1690). To emphasize that it was his own creation, Hevelius dedicated Figure L to the pair, shown as a detail in Fig. 3.1. In atlases published before Hevelius, its stars are shown simply marking the flow of the Milky Way through the area. Ian Ridpath (1989) noted that “Hevelius placed the fox near two other hunting animals, the eagle (the constellation Aquila) and the vulture (which was an alternative identification for Lyra). He explained that the fox was taking the goose to neighbouring Cerberus, another of his inventions.”unnamed before.

names.name: Antares
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name, "like Ares", likening the red colour of this star to its planetary namesake (the Roman Mars), name occurs in the Almagest. Possibly the Greek name goes back to a Sumerian precursor AN.TA.GUB (as suggested by Horowitz).

names.name: Antinous
names.origin: A "sub"-constellation (or asterism) Antinous was created by Ptolemy of Alexandria and published in the Almagest star catalogue 137 CE. It is placed in the constellation of Aquila, The Eagle.

names.name: Apamvatsa
names.origin: Apāmvatsa, "calf of the waters" (or: "the smaller one"), is an Indian star name attested throughout the last millennium. The only indication of the position is Apamvatsa is 5° to the north of Citrā (Spica) in Virgo, attested in several historical documents.

names.name: Apdu
names.origin: Apd(w), pd, The Bird, is an ancient Egyptian constellation from the second millennium BCE; the language is moribunt. There are at least 21 spelling variants throughout the millennia in hierglyphs, and it is probably not any specific bird; might be a goose or falcon or something else. Four star names within the constellation are attested in Ramesside Star Clocks and identified with the area between alpha, beta Per and all of Triangulum. WGSN adopts the name of the constellation for any unspecific spot within its area to preserve an old Egyptian cultural name.

names.name: Arcturus
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name, "the Guard, or Guardian". Reapplied in Early Modern times. As the Greek word, "bear," also came to mean "north," the meaning can ambiguously be "Guardian of the North" and "Guardian of the Bear", referring to the nearby constellation Ursa Major.

names.name: Arin-majlep
names.origin: Arin-majlep, the "replica of the Big Eye", with the Big Eye referring to Altair, is the name of a small asterism of three stars in a row: epsilon, zeta, and omega Aql. WGSN named epsilon Aql after it.

names.name: Arkab Posterior
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period 'urqub al-rami, "the Archer's Achilles Tendon."

names.name: Arkab Prior
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period 'urqub al-rami, "the Archer's Achilles Tendon."

names.name: Arneb
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name al-arnab "the Hare", for Lepus.

names.name: Ascella
names.origin: ascella ("armpit"). Although it appeared in the 1515 Almagest, the name does not appear to have come into common usage until the 20th century after appearing as Ascella in Richard Hinckley Allen's "Star Names Their Lore and Meaning" (1899).

names.name: Asellus Australis
names.origin: From their joint Roman name the Aselli (and also Asini), "the Asses" of "Donkeys", being a translation of these stars' Greek name. Reapplied in Early Modern times, along with the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern".

names.name: Asellus Borealis
names.origin: From their joint Roman name the Aselli (and also Asini), "the Asses" of "Donkeys", being a translation of these stars' Greek name. Reapplied in Early Modern times, along with the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern".

names.name: Ashlesha
names.origin: Āślesā is the Sanskrit name for an asterism in Hydra. It is considered one of the traditional Naksatras (lunar stations).

names.name: Aspidiske
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Greek word π, "little shield", used by Ptolemy in the Almagest in describing several stars in his constellation Argo, that were fixed to the ship for protection and decoration. Ptolemy's shields were in today's Puppis and Vela, but their identification was confused when Argo was divided into the modern Carina, Puppis, and Vela.

names.name: Asterope
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Asuusiha
names.origin: Asu Usiha (Manchu:, Net Stars), a Manchu shamanic constellation. It represents a hunting net to capture sables.

names.name: Athebyne
names.origin: The transliteration Athebyne is one of several renderings of the Arabic asterism name al-dhi bayn, "the (two) wolves" (zeta and eta Draconis) aiming at the Camel's Foal (group of northern asterisms).

names.name: Atik
names.origin: Applied in recent times (also to zeta Per), from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name 'atiq al-thurayya, "the Collarbone of the Pleiades," for omicron and zeta Per, after their location in the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism here

names.name: Atlas
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Atria
names.origin: Contraction of Bayer designation A(lpha) Tri(anguli) A(ustralis). The name is listed as "Alpha Tri. Aust." in 1951 American Nautical Almanac, but listed as "Atria" in 1952 version and subsequent versions.

names.name: Aurwandilsta
names.origin: Aurvandils tá, Aurvandill's Toe, is a Norse constellation from Iceland, documented in Snorri's Edda from the 13th century CE.

names.name: Avior
names.origin: Invented for The Air Almanac of the HM Nautical Almanac Office

names.name: Azelfafage
names.origin: From the Arabic constellation name al-sulahfat, "the Tortoise," for Lyra (corresponding to the Greek image of a tortoise shell for the Lyre's soundboard). Transliterated as Azelfage, a Medieval Latin translator erroneously attributed this constellation name to Cygnus. Then in Early Modern times, the corruption "Azelfafage" was applied as a star name to pi1 Cyg.

names.name: Azha
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name udhi al-na'am, "the Ostrich's Nest," for zeta, rho2,3, eta and tau1 Eri, and epsilon and pi Cet.

names.name: Azmidi
names.origin: The name is an abbreviated misspelling of a Greek term. In the Almagest, the third star in Argo is called "The northernmost of the 2 stars close together over the little shield in the poop." The 'little shield' in Greek is π (Aspidiske), sometimes misspelled Azmidi(ske), and the asterism may or may not consist of stars, while the Almagest lists xi and omicron Pup "above" it. According to Allen (1899) The Century Atlas (1897) by Benjamin E. Smith registers iota Arg (now Car) with the name "Aspidiske".

names.name: Bade
names.origin: Bade, the Funeral Tower, is an Oceanic constellation name from Bali (Indonesia).

names.name: Bagu
names.origin: Bā Gu (Eight Kinds of Crops) is a Chinese constellation consisting of eight stars located within the constellations Lynx, Auriga, and Camelopardalis. It refers to land management officials in charge of rice, millet, barley, wheat, soybean, bean, chestnut, and hemp. It belongs to the asterisms introduced by Gan De and originated during the Han dynasty (roughly 2000 years ago).

names.name: Baijiu
names.origin: Bài Jiù (Broken Mortar) is a Chinese asterism of four stars that represents damaged implement for processing staple food.

names.name: Bake-eo
names.origin: A Marshallese star name for gamma Oph. Pronounced "bakey-yew". Both spellings, "Bake-eo" and "Bake Eo" are accepted. The particle "Eo" simply means "here it is, take it", Bake is the spondylus mussel.

names.name: Baltesha
names.origin: (MUL.)BAL.TEŠ2.A, the Asterism of Dignity, is an ancient Sumerian constellation in CrB.

names.name: Baten Kaitos
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its name for the Arabic Almagest period batn qaitus, "the Sea Monster's Belly."

names.name: Beemim
names.origin: Spelling variations of this name appeared in medieval sources for star 29 in Eridanus in the Almagest (Upsilon3 Eri), with the Alfonsine Tables (1492, Tabule Astronomice Alfonsi Regis) spelling it as "Beemim".

names.name: Beid
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-baid, "the Eggs" for unspecified dim stars around the pre-Islamic Arabian ostrich's nest.

names.name: Bellatrix
names.origin: A Latin name meaning "the Female Warrior", given to alpha Aur in a medieval astrological text (the reason behind this initial application is not fully understood and awaits further findings in corresponding Arabic texts). In late medieval times, bellatrix was transferred to gamma Ori, perhaps by association with the name Bellator, "the Male Warrior", which was used for Orion in other astrological texts.

names.name: Betelgeuse
names.origin: Applied with varied spellings since medieval times, from its pre-Islamic Arabian name yad al-jauza', "the Hand of al-jauza'" (The first medieval transliteration into Latin was bedalgeuze, mistaking the initial Arabic letter as "b" instead of "y." In Early Modern times this corruption was erroneously attributed to the assumed Arabic word "bat" [properly ibt], for "the Armpit" of al-jauza', giving rise to the corruption Betelgeuse" seen today. Thus by Early Modern times both the "y" and "d" of the first part of the pre-Islamic Arabian name had become corrupted.) The pre-Islamic Arabian asterism al-jauza' was a feminine figure represented in the stars of what is today Orion. The origin of its name is unclear (as with nearly all of the ancient group of pre-Islamic Arabian names). The root jwz can mean "middle," and the word al-jauza' is structured as a feminine adjective, thus al-jauza' may mean "the female one, having something about her related to the middle." There have been different speculations as to what the "middle" reference, if that is what it is, could be (for one example). The pre-Islamic Arabians' al-jauza' corresponded to what in other cultures was Gemini among the zodiacal signs. The Arabics subsequently used the indigenous name for both the Greek Orion and Twins, leading to some confusion in star names between the two constellations. An alternative name for the Arabic Almagest period for Orion was al-jabbar, "the Giant" and for Gemini, al-taw'aman, "the Twins."

names.name: Bharani
names.origin: the Indian term (Sanscrit), The Bearer, designates the 2nd of the 27 nakshatras consisting of the three stars 35, 39 and 41 Ari, among which 41 Ari is the brightest. The modern star name was given to the brightest star of the historical constellation.

names.name: Bibing
names.origin: Bibing, The handle of the Net (Lunar Mansion) in the super-constellation of the White Tiger of the West, attested in ancient China for more than 2000 years.

names.name: Bie
names.origin: Biē (River Turtle) is a traditional Chinese asterism. The huge cultural significance of turtles in China can be traced archaeologically to Late Hongshan culture (3300-3000 BCE).

names.name: Biham
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name sa'd al-biham, for theta and nu Peg. A possible meaning for the name is "the Lucky (Stars) of the Young Beasts [lambs, kids, and the like]," but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Blaze Star
names.origin: "Blaze Star" as a nickname for the recurrent nova T CrB has occurred in magazines since 1866. At that time, the physics of novae and supernovae was yet unknown, and the eruption of T CrB in 1866 was actually the first time of a naked-eye transient with spectroscopic evidence for hydrogen in the emission nebula. Recurrent Novae are a rare type of stars; only ten Galactic objects are known. T CrB is the prototype of T CrB-type recurrent novae which are contact binaries composed of a white dwarf orbiting a red giant.

names.name: Bodu
names.origin: Bó Dù (“Textile Ruler”) is a Chinese asterism consisting of two stars, established by the Wuxian tradition during the Han dynasty. WGSN chose to adopt the name according to the Yi Shitong catalog because earlier identifications are highly uncertain.

names.name: Botein
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-butain, "the Little Belly", for delta, and rho Ari.

names.name: Brachium
names.origin: For Bayer (1603), this star is gamma Scorpii with no proper name but in the register for the Scorpius-star chart, he lists "Virgilius brachium" among other (Greek and Arabic) designations for this star. Allen (1899, 368/9) that Vergil had not meant it as a star name but only as a marker for the "claws", so it was never meant as a proper name.

names.name: Bunda
names.origin: Bunda is a Persian lunar mansion.

names.name: Buranun
names.origin: The Sumerian name for the river Euphrates. Euphrates has been honoured with two constellations, independently invented in early modern Europe and ancient Mesopotamia. WGSN picked a star in the ancient constellation.

names.name: Canopus
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name (Ptolemy's spelling), an untranslated proper name that was introduced rather late into Greek astronomy (perhaps in the 2nd century BCE). There seem to be Egyptian influences in the name's development. Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Capella
names.origin: Its ancient Roman name meaning "the She-goat" (but more commonly given, in antiquity, as Capra), after the star's Greek name, "the Goat". Reapplied in recent times. The Roman names Capella, Aselli (for gamma/ delta Cnc), and others in the diminutive form (also in Greek), are likely meant to indicate an atypical use of words, as an animal's name given to a star instead of to the animal (rather than meaning "small" animals or personages).

names.name: Caph
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-kaff al-khadib "the Stained Hand," alternatively and more correctly used for all the brighter stars of today's Cassiopeia (probably alpha, beta, gamma, delta, and epsilon). The pre-Islamic Arabian figure here represented a hand with its finger-tips stained reddish-brown in the traditional Eastern way using henna leaves. al-kaff al-khatdib, in turn, was part of the larger pre-Islamic Arabian asterism kaff althurayya al-yumna al-mabsuta, "the Outstretched Right Hand of the Pleiades." The latter extended from today's Taurus through Perseus into Cassiopeia. A second hand (the Pleiades were a "head" from which two arms or hands radiated) was al-kaff al-jadhma', "the Amputated Hand," in today's Cetus.

names.name: Castor
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name, a character in Greek mythology, the twin of Pollux (beta Gem). Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Castula
names.origin: Castula is Latin for a type of woman's tunic. Bayer (1603, Uranometria) attributes the name "castulum" to Nonius (Portugese scholar Pedro Nunez, 1502-1578), with the Greek alias for a ribbon.

names.name: Cebalrai
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name kalb al-ra'i, "the Shepherd's Dog" (in other traditions alpha Her and 28/29 Cep are given the same name). This dog, together with the shepherd (marked by alpha Oph), and the two lines of stars enclosing the Pasture, and all the dim stellar sheep in that portion of the sky (al-ghanam or al-aghnam for the sheep), seem to form a complete group of pre-Islamic Arabian figures.

names.name: Celaeno
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Cervantes
names.origin: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra (1547-1616) was a famous Spanish writer and author of "El Ingenioso Hidalgo Don Quixote de la Mancha".

names.name: Cexing
names.origin: Cè (Whip) is an ancient Chinese star name representing the horsewhip, located beside the asterism Wangliang and closely associated with both Wangliang and Tiansi. It belongs to the Gān school. "Xing" means star. The ancients sometimes also call it Cexing (whip star) or Tiance (celestial whip). In modern and postmodern literature in English, the name is occasionally used for gamma Cas but this is a late shift, only attested from the 18th century onwards when the Chinese uranography was reworked under Jesuit influence. WGSN corrects the adoption to the Indigenous version.

names.name: Chalawan
names.origin: Chalawan is a mythological crocodile king from a Thai folktale.

names.name: Chamukuy
names.origin: The Yucatec Maya identify Theta Tauri as chamukuy, the name of a small bird.

names.name: Chara
names.origin: Applied in Early Modern times from the Greek word, "joy", that was used by Hevelius in 1690 to name the southern dog (marked by alpha and beta CVn) in his new constellation Canes Vanatici.

names.name: Chertan
names.origin: Applied in recent times from one spelling of the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-khurtan, "the Two Small Ribs (at or near the breast)," for delta and theta Leo. The more common and apparently correct spelling of the lunar mansion name is al-kharatan, of unknown meaning.

names.name: Citalá
names.origin: Citalá means River of stars in the native Nahuat language.

names.name: Copernicus
names.origin: Nicolaus Copernicus or Mikolaj Kopernik (1473-1543) was a Polish astronomer who proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system in his book "De revolutionibus orbium coelestium".

names.name: Cor Caroli
names.origin: The name first appeared in 1673 on the northern half of a pair of celestial hemispheres that accompanied a book called Astroscopium by the English cartographer Francis Lamb. He labelled the star Cor Caroli Regis Martyris, a reference to the fact that King Charles I was beheaded, or ‘martyred’, as Lamb loyally put it (Charles had declared himself ‘martyr of the people’ at his execution).

names.name: Cujam
names.origin: From the Latin word caiam, "club" (in the accusative case, nominative case "caia"), see Kunitzsch and Smart (2006). The Greek term for "club" is already a star name in Eratosthenes (Pamias and Zucker 2013).

names.name: Cursa
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name kursiy al-jauza' al-muqaddam, "the Foremost footstool of aljauza' [today's Orion]," for lambda, beta and psi Eri, and tau Ori.

names.name: Custos
names.origin: Custos Messium, the Harvest Keeper, was a constellation invented in Early Modern Time by the French astronomer Joseph Jérôme de Lalande (1732–1807) who might have punned with the name of his compatriot Charles Messier. Some European astronomers copied and translated it, though. The constellation became obsolete in the depolitisation of the IAU-sky and WGSN only resembles the Keeper, Custos.

names.name: Dabih
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name sa'd aldhabih, for alpha and beta Cap. Possible meanings for the name are "the Lucky (Stars) of the Slaughterer," or, "Sa'd, the Slaughtering One" (this last using Sa'd as an unspecified proper name). However the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Dajiangjunbei
names.origin: , “Celestial Grand General” is an important constellation in ancient China. As the determinative star was already named, WGSN named the northernmost star "The Northern one of The Great General" (Dajiangjunbei).

names.name: Dalim
names.origin: The name was introduced for the star by Piazzi (1814) originating from the Indigenous Arabian asterism al-zalīm, The Ostrich, seen in various stars (e.g. Fomalhaut, theta Eridani)

names.name: Darlugal
names.origin: Derived from Sumerian DAR.LUGAL, The Rooster, an animal first domesticated in China and India, and archaeologically attested in West Asia only since the 2nd millennium BCE for cockfights.

names.name: Deltoton
names.origin: Deltoton (Δ; the letter Delta: delta) is an ancient Greek name variant for the constellation triangulum, probably the original one as "Delta" is the first letter in the ancient Greek term for "dios", the highest god who possesses and rules the stars. In early uranographies, this triangle was considered a sign of the divinity of the starry sky, a divine inscription "written in the stars".

names.name: Deneb
names.origin: "Tail" in Arabic

names.name: Deneb Algedi
names.origin: "Tail of the Goat" in Arabic

names.name: Denebola
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from its name for the Arabic Almagest period dhanab al-asad, "the Lion's Tail."

names.name: Dhanishta
names.origin: one of the Nakshatras, a constellation, depicted as an (unnumbered) multitude of stars

names.name: Dhanuśarāgra
names.origin: Dhanuśarāgra, The Arrow, is an Indian star name found on astrolabes since the 14th century CE for a star in (Greek) Sagittarius.

names.name: Diphda
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-difdi' al-thani, "the Second Frog" (a PsA was the pre-Islamic Arabians' "First Frog," al-difdi' al-awwal).

names.name: Dschubba
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the name for the Arabic Almagest period jabhat al-'aqrab, "the Scorpion's Forehead," for beta, delta, and pi Sco.

names.name: Dubhe
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from the Arabic constellation name al-dubb, "the Bear," for Ursa Major. The spelling in the oldest sources was edubh (corresponding to the Arabic noun with the article al prefixed as e). Afterwards, by corruption, the initial e was transferred to the end of the word: dubhe.

names.name: Dziban
names.origin: Dsiban, from Al Dhibain (the Arabs' title for zeta and eta), has been given by some to this pair [psi1, psi2 Dra].

names.name: Edasich
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-dhikh, "the Male Hyena."

names.name: Electra
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Elgafar
names.origin: This name is a rare transliteration of Arabic al-ghafr (or "El-ġafr"), The Cover. This transliteration was used by Ideler (1809) but is uncommon today except in the Arabic Maghreb (northwest Africa). It is the name of the 15th lunar station (5 Oct).

names.name: Elkurud
names.origin: Early Arab poets referred to a number of anonymous stars as al-furūd, "the solitary ones". Besides this known name, Allen (1899) suggested that al-furūd might have been an old transcriber's error for al-qurūd "the apes", which he rendered "Al Kurūd". Although this idea did not receive scholarly support, WGSN used the rare transliteration Elkurud for this star, as "Furud" was already chosen for zeta CMa.

names.name: Elnath
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-nath, "the Butting (with the horns)," an alternative name for the 1st lunar mansion al-sharatān consisting of beta and gamma Ari (see beta Ari). Some late Arabic authors also applied al-nath as a star name to alpha Ari. In recent times the name, as “Nath,” was wrongly transferred to beta Tau, and subsequently it was completed to “Elnath” (adding the Arabic definite article).

names.name: Eltanin
names.origin: Applied in Early Modern times from the Arabic constellation name al-tinnīn, “the serpent”, for Draco.

names.name: Enduri Senggu
names.origin: Name of the Hedgehog Goddess. She is the guardian of human dwellings and in the sky points head northwards, tail southwards in winter.

names.name: Enif
names.origin: Applied in medieval times, evidently from the Arabic word anf, "nose" (Ptolemy had described this star on the horse's "muzzle"). However, Arabic sources do not mention anf for epsilon Peg, only other terms, hence the ultimate origin of "Enif" remains uncertain.

names.name: Errai
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-ra'i, "the Shepherd". This shepherd, with the sheep he attended (al-aghnam, marked by the various dim stars nearby), and the shepherd's dog (kalb al-ra'i,marked by 28/29 [rho] Cep), seem to form a complete group of pre-Islamic Arabian figures.

names.name: Fafnir
names.origin: Fafnir was a Norse mythological dwarf who turned into a dragon.

names.name: Fang
names.origin: determinitive star of lunar mansion Fang (The Room) whose naming constellation constists of 4 stars according to sources back to the 3rd millennium BCE.

names.name: Fawaris
names.origin: al-Fawāris, "the Riders" is an in indigenous Arabic asterism consisting of at least four stars. WGSN applied the name of the group to one of its members that now preserves (pars pro toto) the Indigenous heritage.

names.name: Felis
names.origin: Felis (The Cat) is the name of a constellation invented by Lalande. The name is applied to one star in the area that the constellation covered.

names.name: Fenmu
names.origin: Fén Mù (Tomb) is an ancient Chinese constellation. The cluster of constellations with that topic can be understood as a celestial projection of funeral rituals.

names.name: Fomalhaut
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period fam al-but al-janubi, "the Mouth of the Southern Fish."

names.name: Formosa
names.origin: Formosa is the historical name of Taiwan used in the 17th century, meaning beautiful in Latin.

names.name: Fulu
names.origin: traditional Chinese single star asterism: an auxiliary road to Gedao; also represents the chief assistant to maintain roads. Gedao (the flying corridor) is a long chain of stars next to the Purple Palace enclosure constellation. Paradoxically, the auxiliary road is considered a single star asterism as attested in several historical star charts (e.g. the famous Suzhou map). Sun and Kistemaker (1997) who studied sources from the Han dynasty (around the year "0" plusminus 200 years) identify zeta Cas with this single star. Another researcher, Sun Shuwei, who dealt with the Xinyixiangfayao Star Map from Su Song (1020-1101 CE) identifies delta Cas. Both is plausible.

names.name: Fumalsamakah
names.origin: Arabic fum al-samakah means "mouth of the fish". The name was considered traditional by the IAU in 2016, although it does not appear in Kunitzsch and Smart (2006) and not in Allen (1899).

names.name: Furud
names.origin: Ultimately from the Arabic word al-furud, "the solitary ones", used in an Arabic poet's allusion to anonymous "solitary stars" around some star hadari. The word was not intended as a name for specific stars as some later Arabic authors supposed. The attempted identity of the "al-furud" stars, like their companion hadari, was variously attributed to stars in today's Centaurus and Columba. The latter stars were included under Canis Maior in the Almagest, leading, in recent times, to the confused assignment of the erroneous "Furud".

names.name: Fuyue
names.origin: traditional Chinese single star asterism: a legendary wise minister of the Yin or Shang dynasty, 18th century BCE. According to Rufus and Tien (1945), sometimes called the invocator (regarding faults). Sun and Kistemaker (1997) quote Sima Qian that Fu Yue was a chancellor of Emperor Wu Ding of the Yin dynasty but they admit that the could also represent a shaman in the royal harem helping to produce sons. The ancient star name is typically identified with the bright star G Sco.

names.name: Gacrux
names.origin: Contraction of Gamma and Crux, appearing in the 1940s.

names.name: Gaja
names.origin: The term "gaja" in Sanskrit means "elephant". Yet, the constellation "Gaja(h)" is not known in India but only in Indonesia. There it is attested in the cultural calendar called Palelintangan where it is found in the intersection between Sunday and the second day of a five-day cycle.

names.name: Gang
names.origin: Gàng (“Shaft”) forms part of the ancient Chinese asterism of Huá Gài (Canopy of the Emperor). Allen (1899) mentions the term as a star name in Cam but WGSN places it in a correcter position.

names.name: Garnet Star
names.origin: Piazzi (1803) named the star Garnet Sidus due to a description by W. Herschel (1773) as "deep garnet red"; the English name is well-established in recent literature and textbooks.

names.name: Genghe
names.origin: Gěnghé (Celestial Lance) is a Chinese constellation of 3 stars. WGSN named the second star in the line.

names.name: Giausar
names.origin: From the Persian word jauzahr, a technical term designating the nodes of the moon's or any planet's orbit. Erroneously applied as a star name to lambda Dra in recent times.

names.name: Gienah
names.origin: A name transferred from gamma Crv in recent times, where the Arabic word janab means "wing" (in the Almagest, both epsilon Cyg and gamma Crv lie on the wings of their respective constellations)

names.name: Ginan
names.origin: Ginan is the Wardaman name of epsilon Cru, from the Northern Territory, Australia. Ginan was found by Mulugurnden (the crayfish), who brought the red flying foxes from the underworld to the sky. The bats flew up the track of the Milky Way and traded the spiritual song with Guyaru, the Night Owl (Sirius). The bats fly through the constellation Scorpius on their way to the Southern Cross, trading songs as they go. The song informs the people about initiation, which is managed by the stars in Scorpius and related to Larawag (who ensures the appropriate personnel are present for the final stages of the ceremony). The colour of the star is reflected as the brownish-red colour of the dilly bag and its association with ceremonial fire.

names.name: Gomeisa
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian surname al-ghumaisa', "the Little Bleary-eyed One ('with a filthy fluid in the corner of the eye')," for alpha CMi. Wrongly transferred to beta CMi in recent times. The original significance of the surname is unknown. Perhaps as an attempt to explain the significance of al-ghumaisa', as well as that of the surname al-<abur, "the One Having Crossed Over [a river, etc.]," for alpha CMa, an Arabic fable developed associating these and other equally enigmatic star names. According to one version of the fable, al-ghumaisa and ai-'abur were sisters, and their brother was suhail (alpha Car). Suhail, in turn, was the suitor of al-jauza' (the feminine pre-Islamic Arabian figure in place of Orion). In coitus, suhail broke the spine of al-jauza', thus killing her, after which suhail fled south. He was followed by his sister al-'abur who "crossed over" the Milky Way (where the two stars now lie in the southern sky). Meanwhile suhail's second sister, al-ghumaisa, was left alone north of the Milky Way, weeping, until her "eyes became bleary." (The pre-Islamic Arabian name for alpha CMa was al-shi'ra, of unknown meaning. Apparently it was developed into a dualis form, al-shi'rayan, to accomodate both alpha CMa and alpha CMi, with the aforementioned "surnames" distinguishing the two.)

names.name: Gouguo
names.origin: Gou Guó (Territory of Dog), is a traditional Chinese asterism that corresponds to the non-Han peoples of northern and northeastern China.

names.name: Grumium
names.origin: A Late Latin word (its correct spelling should be grunnum) meaning "snout" or "muzzle (especially of a pig)", used in the Medieval Latin Almagest in describing this star. The word was applied as a star name in recent times.

names.name: Guansuo
names.origin: Guàn Suo (Coiled Thong), a Chinese constellation of 9 stars in CrB. It resembles a string threaded through a series of copper coins, attested since ancient times.

names.name: Gudja
names.origin: Gudja is the Wardaman name of kappa Ser, from the Northern Territory, Australia. Gudja is a Water Goanna, related to birth and rebirth. It is part of the bright trio of stars in Serpens Caput, which also include Munin the Rock Cod (gamma Ser) and the Mungamungga birthing place (beta Ser), likened to a little hospital. Gudja is involved with the birthing process, which includes sacred ritual practices. The Spiritual Women at the birthing and blessing site in Serpens Caput are connected to the sacred areas of Crux and enacted at Munin Rock and Yinggalarri.

names.name: Gumala
names.origin: Gumala is a Malay word, which means a magic bezoar stone found in snakes, dragons, etc.

names.name: Guniibuu
names.origin: Guniibuu is the Kamilaroi/Euahlayi name for the robin red-breast bird (Petroica boodang). A traditional story links Guniibuu with Gidjirrigaa (Budgerigar) the star kappa Sco.

names.name: Guqi
names.origin: Gu Qí (Drum Flag) is a Chinese asterism consisting of nine stars that originated no later than about 100 BCE. It forms a super-constellation with Hé Gu (River-Drum) and Zuo Qí (Left Flag), as drums and flags were used to transmit signals.

names.name: Hadar
names.origin: From some pre-Islamic Arabian name hadari (an untranslated proper name), for one of a pair of stars, the other one being al-wazn. Sci-A authors ventured to identify these stars as alpha/beta Cen or alpha/beta Col, but exactly what two stars were originally intended, and the significance of their names, is unknown. "Hadar" was arbitrarily applied to beta Cen in recent times.

names.name: Haedus
names.origin: The Almagest star catalogue gives for n Aur: π π beta vμ v omicron π μ (The rearmost of the two stars on the left wrist, which are called 'Haedi'). The Latin term "Haedi" is a translation of Greek v and plural of "Haedus" meaning "young goat(s)".

names.name: Hamal
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name, al-hamal, "the Lamb", for Aries. al-hamal seems to belong to those zodiacal constellation names already known in Arabic times.

names.name: Hassaleh
names.origin: hasa means in Arabic - handsome or good or benefactor, hassa (with doubled s) is from the same Arabic root, has long vowel (second a) and its meaning is "doer of good" or "benefactor", the end of name "-eh" (or "-ah") could mean femininum. Name from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965).

names.name: Hatysa
names.origin: Name of unknown etymology from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965).

names.name: Helvetios
names.origin: Helvetios is the Latin for "the Helvetian" and refers to the Celtic tribe that lived in Switzerland during the Middle Ages.

names.name: Heng
names.origin: Heng is an old Chinese name of a constellation within the super-constellation of Kulou, The Arsenal. The translation is not certain; probably a measuring device.

names.name: Heryibwia
names.origin: Wia, The Boat, is a large ancient Egyptian constellation in Sco & Sgr; “Heryib Wia”, The Middle of the Boat, is a star mentioned in the diagonal star clocks, c. 2300 BCE.

names.name: Heze
names.origin: Name of unknown etymology from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965). It could refer to God, possibly derived from Ezechiel (one of four prophets from Old Testament). Transcription to the Greek language adds "H" to EZE.

names.name: Hoerikwaggo
names.origin: the name of the constellation originally was Mons Mensae (Table Mountain) and not only "table"; this mountain had been called Sea-Mountain by Indigenous ethnics, in the Saan/ Khoe language spelled Huri oaxa, simplified in Africaans Hoerikwaggo.

names.name: Homam
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name sa'd al-humam, for zeta and xi Peg. A possible meaning for the name is "the Lucky (Stars) of the Hero," but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Honores
names.origin: The Latin term "Honores" means honour. A constellation introduced by Bode (1801). He had given a paper in 1790 that this was a joined decision by many European astronomers as a memorial to an extraordinarily generous patron of scientific research and benevolent, peaceful ruler. WGSN considers this message worth to convay even without the dedication to a specific person; we named a star in the feather "Honores" as there is a German proverb "Die Feder ist mächtiger als das Schwert" (the feather is mightier than the sword).

names.name: Hru
names.origin: Hru or Ru means Arrow. The term derives from Sanskrit, but is used as a constellation on the Island of Bali for at least 1300 years.

names.name: Huagai
names.origin: Huá Gài (Canopy of the Emperor) is a Chinese asterism consisting of sixteen stars, divided into two parts: seven stars forming the Huá Gài (“Canopy”) proper and nine forming the Gàng (“Shaft”). The asterism originated within the Gan school during the Han dynasty, around the first century BCE.

names.name: Hydor
names.origin: The IAU-name "Hydor" resembles the original application of this name as a constellation in a vast area of faint stars in antiquity. It fits nicely the Indigenous Arabian constellation of "Safina", Ship. Note that the name "Hydor" was misapplied to a star in Aqr in the recent time. WGSN corrects this mistake. The Greek term "Hydor", Water, originally referred to a huge constellation, depicted around Cetus on ancient globes and described south of Aquarius in Aratus's poem of the 4th century BCE.

names.name: Idigna
names.origin: The Sumerian term for the Tigris river. Tigris has been honoured with two constellations, independently invented in early modern Europe and ancient Mesopotamia. WGSN picked a star in the ancient constellation.

names.name: Iklil
names.origin: the name derives from the Arabic lunar mansion "Iklil" (Arabic), "The ornamented headband" (or: diadem) composed of the 3 stars beta1, delta and pi Sco; here misapplied to rho Sco.

names.name: Imai
names.origin: The Mursi name a line of four stars imai (delta Cru), thaadoi (beta Cru), waar (beta Cen) and sholbi (alpha Cen). Their successive disappearance (heliacal setting) are used to determine when the River Omo will flood (it does this several times) and hence to determine when to plant the annual crop of cowpeas beside it (after the last flood but before the ground dries out). Imai is the Mursi name for the grass that grows along the banks of the river (Rhynchelytrum repens). It is said that when the imai star disappears, the Omo rises high enough to flatten the imai grass.

names.name: Intercrus
names.origin: Intercrus means "between the legs" in Latin style, referring to the star's position in the constellation Ursa Major.

names.name: Izar
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic word izwar, "girdle" or "loin cloth", being a later version of the original term al-mi)zar used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star.

names.name: Jabbah
names.origin: the name was considered popular by WGSN as mentioned in Allen (1899): "in the Century Cyclopaedia, perhaps from its being one of the mansil Iklil al Jabbah."

names.name: Jian
names.origin: Jiàn (Erect) means “to set up” or “to erect,” as in raising a wooden pole or a flagstaff. It is an ancient Chinese constellation, attested since the 4th century BCE.

names.name: Jiantai
names.origin: Jiàn Tái (Clepsydra Terrace) is a Chinese constellation of 4 stars, a symbol of astronomical timekeeping and musical pitch calibration.

names.name: Jishui
names.origin: traditional Chinese single star asterism: translations of the term are "Bilgewater", "a store of water to make wine", or "accumulated water (held in by dikes for future use)". It refers to a faint star in Gemini or Perseus that is idenfied differently by modern authors. Sun and Kistemaker (1997) from Han sources and Sun Shuwei (Stellarium) from a medieval source both suggest o Gem while Xu et al. (2000) identify lambda Persei.

names.name: Jiu
names.origin: Jiù (Mortar) and Nèichu (Inner Pestle) are a Chinese super-constellation attested since Han Dynasty.

names.name: Jordanus
names.origin: Jordanus was used as a constellation name by Plancius in his 1612 celestial map, which introduced some uniting elements for Europeans fighting each other in the early modern spirit of an "under one sky"-philosophy.

names.name: Junnanmen
names.origin:
Jūn Nán Mén ("Southern Millitary Gate") is a Chinese constellation, simplified: Junnanmen. It is the name of a Chinese single-star asterism that WGSN preserves in its earliest version (before Tang Dynasty), identified with phi And."Junnanmen" is assigned to the primary of the phi And (HR 335, HIP 5434, HD 6811) binary system, i.e.
phi And A (HD 6811A).

names.name: Kaffaljidhma
names.origin: Arabic, al-kaf al-jaðmā ('the cut-short hand') is given as a star name in Allen (1899) with reference to an Arabic name for the asterism of Cetus's Head.

names.name: Kaffalmusalsala
names.origin: Arabic desciption of a Greek star name. The Arabic term means "Hand of the Chained Woman"; originating from the Almagest "Hand of Andromeda", originally designating a group of three stars.

names.name: Kalasungsang
names.origin: On Bali (Indonesia) "Kala" means "demon" and "sungsang" means "upside down". Originally, the term is from Sanskrit, dark/ death or time. The daemon reminds us not to waste time.

names.name: Kamelos
names.origin: "Kamelos" is Greek for camel, a pun with the name of the constellation "Camelopardalis" whose Latin term is a Greek loanword, literally meaning "checkered camel" = giraffe. On this base, Jacob Bartsch proposed 1624 "Camelus Rebeccae" as an alternative name for the constellation Camelopardalis, a reference to the story of Abraham's daughter-in-law, Rebecca.

names.name: Kang
names.origin: determinitive star of lunar mansion Kang (The Neck) whose naming constellation constists of 4 stars according to sources back to the 3rd millennium BCE

names.name: Kaus Australis
names.origin: Arbitrarily applied in recent times, together with the Latin distinctions of "middle," "southern," and "northern" (for lambda Sgr), from the pre-Islamic Arabian (and later Arabic) constellation name al-qaus, "the Bow." For the pre-Islamic Arabians, al-qaus was marked by the curved line of stars xi2, o, pi, d, rho and u Sgr (corresponding to what in other cultures was Sagittarius among the zodiacal signs). The Arabics used the indigenous name for the Greeks' Archer, alternatively translated as al-rami.

names.name: Kaus Borealis
names.origin: Arbitrarily applied in recent times, together with the Latin distinctions of "middle," "southern," and "northern" (for lambda Sgr), from the pre-Islamic Arabian (and later Arabic) constellation name al-qaus, "the Bow." For the pre-Islamic Arabians, al-qaus was marked by the curved line of stars xi2, o, pi, d, rho and u Sgr (corresponding to what in other cultures was Sagittarius among the zodiacal signs). The Arabics used the indigenous name for the Greeks' Archer, alternatively translated as al-rami.

names.name: Kaus Media
names.origin: Arbitrarily applied in recent times, together with the Latin distinctions of "middle," "southern," and "northern" (for lambda Sgr), from the pre-Islamic Arabian (and later Arabic) constellation name al-qaus, "the Bow." For the pre-Islamic Arabians, al-qaus was marked by the curved line of stars xi2, o, pi, d, rho and u Sgr (corresponding to what in other cultures was Sagittarius among the zodiacal signs). The Arabics used the indigenous name for the Greeks' Archer, alternatively translated as al-rami.

names.name: Kautoki
names.origin: The name means "handle (kau) of the adze (toki)" and describes an asterism from the Polynesian island of Kapingamarangi.

names.name: Keid
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qaid, "the Egg Shells," for unspecified stars around the pre-Islamic Arabian ostrich's nest.

names.name: Kenemu
names.origin: (Stars of) Kenmu, 17th decan in ancient Egyptian astral science, heliacal rise in month Peret, represented by a small group of stars around rho1 Sgr.

names.name: Khambalia
names.origin: The Coptic (Egyptian) term Khambalia means "Crooked-clawed" (perhaps designating an agricultural device or symbol of secret knowledge); it was used in mantic texts for the star in the foot of Virgo.

names.name: Khepdenreret
names.origin: Khepdenreret, the Buttocks of the Hippopotamus (goddess) Reret, is a star name from ancient Egypt documented in the Ramesside Star Clocks from around 1200 BCE

names.name: Kitalpha
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name qit'at al-faras, "the Section of the Horse," for Equuleus. Ptolemy had ππ μ, "the First Half of the Horse," for the constellation, because it shows only half the figure (as with the constellations Taurus, Pegasus, and the Greek ship Argo).

names.name: Kochab
names.origin: Applied to beta UMi in Early Modern times and of uncertam derivation. It is probably from one of the names Alrucaba, Rucaba, etc., that were first applied to theta UMa, then to alpha UMi, in medieval times. However, the name may also be from the Arabic word kaukab, or the Hebrew word kokhabh, both meaning "star."

names.name: Kornephoros
names.origin: From the Greek word, "club-bearer", mentioned in one Early Modern study as a name for the constellation Hercules. Properly it is of mythological rather than astronomical significance, for Ptolemy's constellation here was "the Kneeler", described without a club. "Kornephoros" was applied as a star name in recent times.

names.name: Kraz
names.origin: Name of unknown etymology from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965).

names.name: Kui
names.origin: Kui, The Legs, is an ancient Chinese constellation with 16 stars, belonging to the 28 Lunar Mansions in China, with a very long history. Its determinative star used to be zeta And for many centuries but it was changed to eta And in Qing Dynasty.

names.name: Kulou
names.origin: "Kulou" means arsenal and storied building. It is a super-constellation in the area of modern Cen/Lup created in ancient China, dating back to the 2nd century BCE.

names.name: Kurhah
names.origin: Applied in recent times from one vocalization of its pre-Islamic Arabian name: al-qurha, "the White Spot on the Forehead of a Horse." However, the original Arabic script for the name can be read and vocalized in other ways with various meanings.

names.name: La Superba
names.origin:
In 1868 Secchi used "superba" as an adjective to describe the star Y CVn, not as a proper name of the star.
However, in 1876 Birmingham seems to have borrowed from Secchi this term and used it as a proper name of the star.
As a consequence, in 1877 Secchi himself adopted the same name.
Agnes Clerke attributed the term to Secchi, without distinguishing between the adjective and the name.
In principle, it should be attributed to both Secchi and Birmingham, in my opinion.

names.name: Lang-Exster
names.origin: "Lang" is an Malayan/ Indonesian term meaning "hornbill", "Exster" is a Dutch word meaning "magpie" and both terms were used as name for the newly defined constellation in Early Modern Age by the Dutch sailors (de Houtman 1603) who artificially created the constellation as "Indian Magpie" referring to a species of bird with a strong cultural significance for the indigenous people they met (e.g. Dayak). The star is a spectroscopic binary which is why it makes sense to give it a double-name for the visible dot; the name may be split for the components later.

names.name: Larawag
names.origin: Larawag is the Wardaman name of epsilon Sco, from the Northern Territory, Australia. Larawag is part of a procession of beings along the curve of stars in Scorpius, acting as the signal watcher, noting when only legitimate participants are present and in view of the ceremony. He gives the “All clear” signal, allowing the secret part of the ceremony to continue. This procession is related to the bats that carry Ginan.

names.name: Leepwal
names.origin: Ļeepwal is the name for zeta Cen in Marshallese. Original spelling Ļeepwal. Pronounced leyepwal, the first "l" being pronounced with the back of the tongue raised (velarized) and the root of the tongue retracted (pharyngealized) so as to elongate the oral cavity, thereby giving the consonant a "heavier" or "darker" sound.

names.name: Leidian
names.origin: Léi Diàn (Thunder and Lightning) is a Chinese constellation that is so called because it vanishes as soon as it appears; it has no correlation with meteorology.

names.name: Lembu
names.origin: "Lintang Lěmbu" means Ox/Bull/Cow Constellation, representing an animal to pull carts & chariots. It is found in the calendar series Palelintangan used for at least 1300 years on the islands of Java and Bali, Indonesia.

names.name: Lesath
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the Greek term "(foggy) conglomeration," used by Ptolemy in the Tetrabiblos in describing several nebulous sky objects (in the present case, probably the open cluster M7). Ptolemy's term was translated by the Arabs as al-latkha, "the Spot." This word in turn became transliterated and corrupted in Medieval Latin to alascha, which was used in astrological texts in connection with Scorpius' tail. In Early Modern times, the derivation of alascha was erroneously attributed to the Arabic word las'a, "sting, or bite (of a poisonous animal)," rather than to al-latkha. Subsequently the erroneous word, written as "Lesath," was applied as a star name to u Sco (and in recent times, also to lambda Sco).

names.name: Libertas
names.origin: Libertas is Latin for "liberty". Liberty refers to social and political freedoms, and a reminder that there are people derived of liberty in the world even today. The constellation Aquila represents an eagle - a popular symbol of liberty.

names.name: Ligong
names.origin: Ligong denoted a secondary or temporary palace situated apart from the principal palace and used for the ruler’s temporary residence, repose, and private life.

names.name: Lilii Borea
names.origin: Lacaille used the now obsolete constellation Lilium (The Lily) and named this star "the northern one of the Lily", in Latin: Lilii Borea. see also "Lilium" in the ASE.

names.name: Lintangkumba
names.origin: Lintang in Bahasa Indonesia means asterism; 'kumba' in Balinese is a vessel with sacred water; it derives from Sanskrit (kumbha), jar or pitcher. In both Indian and Indonesian cultures, it is a name for the constellation in Aquarius. In India, it also designates the rāśi (zodiac sign).

names.name: Lumbung
names.origin: The term "Lumbung" is inherited from Malay, Proto-Malayo-Polynesian, designating a quickly set up rice barn or granary. The constellation of Lumbung is attested for ~1300 years in the cultural calendar and associated with Wednesday and the third day of an Oceanic market cycle.

names.name: Maasym
names.origin: From the Arabic word al-mi'sam, "the wrist," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing o Her. Wrongly transferred to lambda Her in Early Modern times.

names.name: Maenalus
names.origin: Mons Maenalus is an early modern European constellation or asterism introduced by Hevelius (1690), setting a celestial memorial for a mountain in the central Peloponnese, Greece.

names.name: Mago
names.origin: Mago is a National Park in Ethiopia noted for its giraffes. The star also happens to be in the constellation of Camelopardis (the giraffe).

names.name: Magur
names.origin: MA2.GUR8, The Boat/Ship, is a constellation south of Sgr. It’s identification is given between Cap, Mic, CrA and southern Sgr. As certainty can only be achieved for Late Babylonian sources, WGSN picked a faint star close to the one which represents the Egyptian Boat-constellation.

names.name: Mahasim
names.origin: Arabic al-mi şam "the wrist", was used for lambda Her by Bayer by misreading the Almagest (and its 1515 Latin translation) where the wrist is designated o Her. Allen 1899, 245 mentions that the 16th century Latin Almagest translation used the (misspelled) variant “Mahasim” for theta and eta Aurigae.

names.name: Maia
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Marfik
names.origin: Applied since medieval times from the Arabic word al-marfiq, "the elbow," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star. While the medieval transliteration was marsic (with a confusion of f and the long-shaped s), Marfik is an improved spelling of recent times.

names.name: Markab
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the name for the Arabic Almagest period mankib al-faras, "the Horse's Shoulder," for beta Peg. Wrongly transferred to alpha Peg in late medieval times.

names.name: Markeb
names.origin: Evidently from the Arabic word markab, "a ship or any vehicle," presumably standing for the Greek constellation name Argo. However, Arabic sources do not mention markab for Argo, only al-safina ("the Ship"), hence the ultimate origin of the name remains a mystery. "Markeb" was applied as a star name to rho Pup in medieval times, to kappa Pup in Early Modern rimes, and finally to kappa Vel in recent times when Argo was divided into its four modern constellations

names.name: Marsic
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from the Arabic word al-marfiq, "the elbow," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star.

names.name: Matar
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name sa'd matar for eta and o Peg. Its meaning is unknown. matar has been translated as "rain," and as a common noun in Arabic, al-matar does mean "the rain." However, lack of the definitive article al- for the star points to a use of the word in a sense different from the common noun.

names.name: Matrichakra
names.origin: Mātrīcakra, The Circle, is an Indian name for CrB; the Sanskrit term occurs on historical globes and astrolabes.

names.name: Mebsuta
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name dhira' al-asad almabsuta, "the Lion's Outstretched Paw," for one of the two pairs alpha/beta Gem or alpha/beta CMi. These pairs were assigned to the larger pre-Islamic Arabian asterism al-asad, but there is no unanimity in the Arabic sources as to which pair was the "outstretched" or "folded" paw. "Mebsuta" was arbitrarily applied as a star name to epsilon Gem in recent times. In its indigenous location stretching from parts of Gemini all the way into Virgo, the pre-Islamic Arabian al-asad, "the Lion," corresponded to what in other cultures was Leo among the zodiacal signs. Subsequently the Arabs used the indigenous name for the smaller Greek Lion (Leo).

names.name: Megrez
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period maghriz al-dubb al-akbar, "the Root (of the tail) of the Greater Bear."

names.name: Meissa
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-maisan, for either gamma or xi Gem. The meaning of the name is uncertain. It may mean "the Sparkling One," referring to a star, or "the Proudly Marching One," referring to a person. Together, gamma and xi Gem composed the pre-Islamic Arabian 6th lunar mansion alhan'a. The nearby stars lambda, 1, and 2 Ori composed the adjacent 5th lunar mansion al-haq'a. Due to confusion between these two parent lunar mansions in a late Arabic source, "Meissa" was wrongly applied to lambda Ori (rather than to gamma or xi Gem) in recent times. "Meissa" (without n at the end) corresponds to pre-Islamic Arabian almaisa', a variant form of al-maisan.

names.name: Mekbuda
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name dhira' al-asad al-maqbuqa, "the Lion's Folded Paw". Arbitrarily applied as a star name to zeta Gem in recent times.

names.name: Meleph
names.origin: Bayer (1603) quotes Arabic designations Melleff and Meeleph for this star (among others) which was adopted by other astronomers (e.g. Riccioli) and goes back to the Arabic term Al Ma'laf, The Stall (a variant of the Greek Manger).

names.name: Menkalinan
