names.origin: Applied in recent times from its Arabic name mankib dhi l-(inan, "the Shoulder of the Reinholder".

names.name: Menkar
names.origin: From the Arabic word al-minkhar, "the nostrils," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing lambda Cet. Wrongly applied as a star name to alpha Cet (properly on the "jaw") in a Medieval Latin star table.

names.name: Menkent
names.origin: Applied in recent times and possibly coined from the Arabic word mankib, "shoulder" (in some recent transliterations: menkib; Ptolemy described this star on the right "shoulder" of the Centaur), plus the Latinized "Kentaurus" for the Arabic constellation name qanturis. Hence this name could be of similar construction to the abbreviation for alpha Cen: "Rigil Kent."

names.name: Menkib
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its pre-Islamic Arabian name mankib al-thurayya, "the Shoulder of the Pleiades," for its location in the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism here.

names.name: Merak
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period maraqq al-dubb al-akbar, "the Flank (or Groin) of the Greater Bear."

names.name: Merga
names.origin: A Latin word meaning "reaping hook," used in a Early Modern discussion of the constellation Bootes. According to this discussion, some classical sources mentioned a reaping hook held in Bootes' hand opposite the staff. Subsequently the word was applied as a star name to hBoo.

names.name: Meridiana
names.origin: The Latin-Arabic name "Alfecca meridiana" is mentioned in Allen (1899, 173). There, it is attributed to "Reduan" (sic!) = Ali bin Radwan's commentary to his Tetrabiblos translation (10th century). Arabic nayyir al-fakka "the bright (star) of the broken (dish)" in analogy to the Arabic term for CrB. WGSN chose only the second (Latin) term: "Meridiana", the southern (one of the two Alfeccas).

names.name: Merope
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Mesarthim
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the Arabic lunar mansion name al-sharatan, for beta and gamma Ari. From the numerous medieval lists of the Arabic lunar mansions (all in Latin transliteration), the Early Modern scholar Johannes Bayer grasped the form Sartai, and used it for the three brighter stars alpha, beta and gamma Ari. Bayer also erroneously explained Sartai as from the Hebrew word mesharethim, "servants", rather than from al-sharatan. Subsequently, Bayer's erroneous word, written as "Mesarthim", was applied as a star name.

names.name: Miaplacidus
names.origin: Applied in recent times, and of unknown astronomical significance. The first element, Mia-, is unexplained. The second element is the Latin adjective placidus, meaning "calm, gentle" (here in the masculine form).

names.name: Mimosa
names.origin: Applied in recent times, and of unknown astronomical significance. It is from the Latin word mimus, "an actor", and is otherwise known as the genus name for certain tropical plants.

names.name: Minchir
names.origin: Minchir appeared in Bode's 1801 Uranographia rooting in the Arabic term minkhar ash-shujā "the nostril brave one" in Hydra.

names.name: Minelauva
names.origin: The 13th Arabic lunar station bears the name) Al- Awwā, The bend. It consists of 5 stars: beta, eta, gamma, delta and epsilon Vir. "Auva" or "Minelauva" are mediaeval transliterations of this name that now names one of its stars.

names.name: Mintaka
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian (and Arabic) asterism name mintaqat al-jauza', "the Belt (or Girdle) of al-jauza'", for delta, epsilon, and zeta Ori.

names.name: Mira
names.origin: Its Latin name since Early Modern times meaning "the Amazing One", as taken from Historiola Mirae Stellae - the title of a work describing the amazing variability of this star (written by Hevelius in 1662).

names.name: Mirach
names.origin: Ultimately from the Arabic word al-mi)zar, "the girdle" or "loin cloth", used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star. The correct transliteration of the word in the Medieval Latin Almagest was mizar, which was occasionally misspelled as mirac, mirat, etc. These corruptions, taken as proper names for beta And, were correctly attributed to al-mi)zar by Early Modern scholars. Subsequently one of the misspellings, "Mirach", gained more popularity over the correct "Mizar", to beome the preferred modern name.

names.name: Miram
names.origin: perhaps a misspelling of the Arabic term mi sam, The Wrist, which was used for naming kappa Per "Misam" in the CSN.

names.name: Mirfak
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its pre-Islamic Arabian name mirfaq al-thurayya, "the Elbow of the Pleiades," for its location in the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism here.

names.name: Mirzam
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its Arabic name al-mirzam, of unknown meaning. The Arabs also gave the name to beta CMi, and sometimes to gamma Ori. Each al-mirzam star preceded the rising of a brighter star (our Sirius, Procyon, and Betelgeuse, respectively), which probably connects to the unknown meaning.

names.name: Misam
names.origin: the Arabic term mi sam, The Wrist, was originally a name of chi Per (Almagest: "the right hand" of the Hero) and considered the Wrist of Thurayya (the Pleiades) for the Arabs.

names.name: Mizar
names.origin: Ultimately from the Arabic word al-maraqq, "the Groin," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing beta UMa. Correct transliterations of almaraqq in the Medieval Latin Almagest were mirac and mirach. However, Early Modern scholars confused these words with the Arabic word mi'zar, which had equally been transliterated and corrupted in Latin as mirac, mirach, etc. Subsequently the mistaken mi'zar, written as "Mizar," was applied as a star name to beta UMa, and it became transferred to zeta UMa in late Early Modern times.

names.name: Mothallah
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name al-muthallath, "the Triangle," for Triangulum.

names.name: Muliphein
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the Arabic names hadari and al-wazn. In Arabic discussions of these names it came to be said that they were muhlifan, meaning "two [things] causing dispute [in this case as to these stars' identification] and the swearing of an oath". From this usage, al-muhlifan was wrongly taken as a name for hadari and al-wazn together. Transliterated and further mutilated as "Muliphein", the name was arbitrarily applied to the single star gamma CMa in recent times.

names.name: Muning
names.origin: Muning, "the Small Rock Cod," is a name for two stars (gamma and beta Ser) in Serpens from the Australian Wardaman people whose Elders approved the name for gamma Ser.

names.name: Muphrid
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the ancient Arabic name for alpha Boo: al-simak al-ramih, "the Lance-bearing simak" (the meaning of simak is uncertain). It seems that later Arabic poets expanded upon this name by making mention of some separate "lance" (al-rumh) that accompanied the star alpha Boo. Subsequent Arabs attempted to identify this fictitious lance with actual stars, sometimes saying it was eta Boo with nearby stars, sometimes saying it was "eta Boo alone" (where "alone", in arabic, is written mufradan). From these discussions came, with a slight copying mistake in the Arabic, the erroneous Arabic name mufrad al-ramih, roughly translating as "the Isolated Single One of the Lance-Bearer". With a wrong vocalization and with abbreviation, this erroneous name, as "Muphrid", was applied in recent times.

names.name: Muscida
names.origin: Almagestum 1515: "illa quae est supra extremitatem Musciae" - Bayer (1603) "in naso, barbaris muscida." - attributed to "Barbarians"

names.name: Musica
names.origin: Musica is Latin for "music".

names.name: Naga
names.origin: Sanskrit, nāgá, means “large snake” or "serpent". Languages like Iban, Indonesian, Italian, Javanese, Malay, Marano, Portuguese, Tagalog and Yakan borrow the term; Japanese "naga" means "long"; German "Nagel" (nail) and English "naked" are derived from homophonous Sanskrit "nāga" for gold/ iron/ metal.

names.name: Nahn
names.origin: "Nahn", the Persian term for "Nose", given to xi Cnc in the NASA Memorandum by Rhoads (1971).

names.name: Nandou
names.origin: Nándou (Southern Dipper) is a Chinese Lunar Mansion, attested for at least 2500 years: one of the oldest asterisms in China.

names.name: Naos
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the word, Greek for the "ship", used in one Early Modern discussion as a name for the ancient constellation Argo (since divided into Puppis, Carina, and Vela).

names.name: Nashira
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian name sa<d nashira, for gamma and delta Cap. Its meaning is unknown. As originally applied, gamma was "Nashira Prima" and delta was "Nashira Posterior."

names.name: Neichu
names.origin: Nèichu (Inner Pestle) is a three-star Chinese asterism that forms a super-constellation with Jiù (Mortar); they are attested for more than 2000 years.

names.name: Nekkar
names.origin: Applied in recent times from a misreading of the Arabic constellation name al-baqqar, "the Ox-driver", for Boötes.

names.name: Nembus
names.origin: Name appears in Bayer's (1603) Uranometria for Upsilon Per (later designated 51 And), which he states is of Arab origin, however the name appears to be Latin not Arabic. From the description it appears that the name appears to be connected with the adamntine harpe sword Perseus used to decapitate Medusa.

names.name: Nganurganity
names.origin: Nganurganity [ anu ̊ani ̊] is the "Jacky lizard" in the culture of the Boorong, a clan of the indigenous Maligundidj people of northwestern Victoria in Australia, who saw it as an ancestral figure who fights the moon, flanked by two wives, represented by stars on either side of him (delta CMa and epsilon CMa). The Moon is Mityan, the quoll. Mityan fell in love with one of the wives of Unurgunite and tried to lure her away. Unurgunite discovered Mityan’s trickery and attacked him, leading to a great fight in which Mityan was defeated. The Moon has been wandering the heavens ever since, the scars of the battle still visible on his face as maria. One of the wives (delta CMa) lies further away from Unurgunite and is closer to the Moon than the other wife (epsilon CMa). This is the wife Mityan tried to lure away. The name was listed as Unurgunite in Stanbridge(1857/61), for initial ng-, which does not occur in English, was typically ignored in transcription of that era. WGSN corrects the spelling.

names.name: Niandao
names.origin: Niăn Dào (Imperial Passageway) is a private way for the emporer for harmonious journeys. WGSN represents it by its determinative star.

names.name: Nihal
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name al-nihal "the Camels Beginning to Quench Their Thirst" for alpha, beta, gamma and delta Lep.

names.name: Ninnisig
names.origin: Ninnisig and Erragal are two Sumerian gods associated with the pair of stars, Ninnisig is the goddess who is butcher of the highest temple (name honours a profession).

names.name: Nunki
names.origin: mulNUN.KI or mulNUNKI = the star or constellation of Eridu where Eridu is one of the first big cities known. Archealogical proofs date back to the 3rd millennium (Sumer). It is located at the southern coast of Mesopotamia. The identification of the star or asterism is highly uncertain: it is often identified with Canopus and adjacent areas or "somewhere in Argo". mulNUN.KI is listed in MUL.APIN and there, it seems to refer to the area of Aquarius with unknown identification (Canopus not excluded) but the identification with other Babylonian texts seems to propose only in the northern part of modern Argo, i.e. Vela. The Euphratean name "Nunki" was mentioned and associated with Sigma Sgr in Robert Brown, Jr. (1892, Proceedings of the Society of Biblical Archaeology, Volume 14, p. 298; "Nun-ki", "Prince-of-the-Earth"), and its use diffused through the 20th century after being mentioned in Richard Hinckley Allen's (Star Names, their lore and meaning, p. 359). The modern Nunki is, thus, not identical with the Sumerian one; it is one of the many misapplications.

names.name: Nusakan
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the collective pre-Islamic Arabian name al-nasaqan, "the Two Lines [of stars]" for two asterisms in today's Hercules, Serpens, Ophiuchus, and Lyra. al-nasaqan originally marked the boundaries of the pre-Islamic Arabian 'al-rauda, "the Pasture". These boundaries were "the Northern Line" al-nasaq al-sha'ami, and "the Southern Line" al-nasaq al-yamani.

names.name: Nüchuang
names.origin: Nu Chuáng (Women’s Bed) is a small asterism consisting of only three stars that dates back to around 100 BCE and belongs to the Shi school.

names.name: Okab
names.origin: Zeta and Epsilon Aquilae together bore the traditional name Deneb el Okab, from an Arabic term Dhanab al- uqāb "the tail of the eagle".

names.name: Pabilsang
names.origin: Pabilsag is the oldest name of the constellation Sagittarius; a Sumerian god, depicted as a mixed creature (centaur-like with additional scorpion-tail and bird features) with bow and arrow; this constellation was taken over and “simplified” by the Greeks. WGSN picked a star in his eye.

names.name: Pagru
names.origin: Akkadian Pagru, "body" or "corpse," is commonly translated "The Dead Man", attested as a constellation in MUL.APIN which dates between 1350 and 1150 BCE, and has been used through the entire 1st millennium BCE.

names.name: Paikauhale
names.origin: Au-haele, Hokū-‘ula and Paikauhale are documented as three stars in a line, running from north to south. Two of the most reliable sources—Mary Puku‘i and Rubellite Johnson—both identify Hokū-‘ula as Antares (alpha Sco), which makes Au-haele Alniyat (sigma Sco) and Paikauhale tau Sco.

names.name: Paradys
names.origin: In Dutch around 1600, two spelling versions of the Apus-bird existed. WGSN decided to take the first part of the earliest written witness, Paradys-vogel (Plancius 1598), to name the main star of the constellation.

names.name: Paushna
names.origin: Pausna is another name for Revati, a goddess that names the 27th Vedic nakshatra.

names.name: Peacock
names.origin: Invented for The Air Almanac of the HM Nautical Almanac Office

names.name: Phact
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic word fakhita, "ring dove," used in connection with the constellation Cygnus in a Early Modern discussion of Arabic bird names.

names.name: Phecda
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period fakhidh al-dubb al-akbar, "the Thigh of the Greater Bear."

names.name: Pherkad
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the singular form of the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism name al-farqadan, "the Two Calves," for beta and gamma UMi.

names.name: Pherkad Minor
names.origin: One of Piazzi's star names following the schema of naming a faint visual neighbour in reference to the visually more striking star in a constellation.

names.name: Phyllon Kissinou
names.origin: Contemporary modern astronomers have used the nickname "Kissin"; therefore, the real name was made official. The term originates from the phrase " v (phyllon kissinou, an ivy leaf)" in Ptolemy's Almagest. The star might be "multiple or double" according to SIMBAD, so long double name for the visible dot in the sky might be split up to the components later.

names.name: Piautos
names.origin: piautos (π) is a composition from Greek autos ("self") and Coptic pi- ("that") meaning "the same one". It occurred in a Coptic manuscript on lunar stations. Coptic is the ancient Egyptian language written in Greek letters, but lunar stations were uncommon for both the Greek and Egyptian culture. Hence, the origin of this term remains unknown.

names.name: Pili
names.origin: Pī Lì (Thunderbolt) is a five-star Chinese constellation, which forms a super-constellation with Yunyu (clouds & rain) and Leidian (thunder and lightning).

names.name: Ping
names.origin: Píng, the Screen in front of a toilet, is a Chinese constellation

names.name: Pipirima
names.origin: There are many versions of a widespread Polynesian story of two children fleeing their uncaring parents to become two shining stars, the stars themselves being variously recorded as Castor and Pollux (alpha and beta Gem), Shaula and Lesath (lambda and upsilon Sco), zeta and theta Sco, and mu¹ and mu² Sco as well as [possibly] omega¹ and omega² Sco. In Tahiti, Pipiri was the twin brother of Rehua: Pipiri ma refers to the two together, ma "with, and" being used after names to mean "et al.". Calderon identifies the two children as mu¹ and mu² Sco, their mother being Shaula (lambda Sco) and their father Lesath (upsilon Sco).

names.name: Pipit
names.origin: Among the Kendayan (Dayak Kenayatn) people of West Kalimantan province, Borneo, Indonesia, the star nu Pup is identified as "Pipit".

names.name: Pleione
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Polaris
names.origin: A Latin adjective meaning "of the pole" (related to the noun polus, "the pole"). Applied as a star name to alpha UMi in Early Modern times, it reflects the star's temporary proximity to the north celestial pole.

names.name: Polaris Australis
names.origin: the term literally means "South Pole" and was first used for the star in the 18th century.

names.name: Polis
names.origin: the term in Coptic means "a foal." It was originally used for stars in the bow of the Archer but was moved over time.

names.name: Pollux
names.origin: This is the classical Latin form of its ancient Greek name, a character in Greek mythology, the twin of Castor (alpha Gem). Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Pongaponga
names.origin: Pongaponga (“nostrils”) is a star name from the island of Pukapuka (South Pacific) for the visual double star epsilon1 (4) Lyr and epsilon2 (5) Lyr. WGSN applies the name to epsilon1 Lyr A.

names.name: Porrima
names.origin: The name of a Roman goddess, one of several mythological names mentioned in connection with the constellation Virgo. Applied as a star name in recent times.

names.name: Praecipua
names.origin: Piazzi (1814) in his star catalogue introduced this proper name for the star because Hevelius (1690) had added the adjective "praecipua" (Chief) as a description of this star.

names.name: Prima Hyadum
names.origin: the Latin term occurs first in Flamsteed (1729) but is based on the Arabic idea to enumerate the stars in the cluster; in Arabic it was Awwal ad-Dabarān, The First of Dabarān (the group from which the star name "Aldebaran" derives).

names.name: Procyon
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name, "the One Preceding the Dog", referring to its rising shortly before the "Dog Star", Sirius. Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Propus
names.origin: Applied in Early Modern times from the Greek word π π, "forward foot", used by Ptolemy in the Almagest in describing this star.

names.name: Protome
names.origin: Protome, the Bust, is the original name of this constellation from Roman time when Greek was still the language of science. The reasons for this invention are not preserved, but mythology later added.

names.name: Pulcherrima
names.origin: The Latin name translates to "most beautiful" or "loveliest," referring to its striking, contrasting colors; it was introduced by F. Struve in 1837.

names.name: Puwuh Atarung
names.origin: Puwuh Atarung means "battling quails", birds that are crucial poultry source of nutritious animal protein (meat and eggs). Their constellation has been used on Bali since 700 CE.

names.name: Qedty
names.origin: Qedty (kdty), The Two Nets, is an Egyptian constellation, used in decan star clocks.

names.name: Qigong
names.origin: Qī Gong (Seven Excellencies) is a Chinese asterism composed of seven stars; WGSN named the determinative star after the constellation.

names.name: Quadrans
names.origin: Quadrans Muralis is an obsolete constellation invented in 1795 by the French astronomer Jérôme Lalande. WGSN decided to commemorate this constellation as it is the root of the name of the Quadrantide meteor shower that peaks in the first days of January.

names.name: Ramus
names.origin: Ramus, The Branch (of golden apples), is an addition to the early modern asterism Cerberus in Hercules. The name occurs in Bayer (1603) as a term but in depiction only later.

names.name: Ran
names.origin: Ran is the Norse goddess of the sea, who stirs up the waves and captures sailors with her net.

names.name: Rana
names.origin: Rana is Latin "The Frog". There are several stars named "frog" in the Arabic culture but at different places. WGSN placed the name at that constellation of the river.

names.name: Rangifer
names.origin: Rangifer, the Reindeer, is an extinct constellation first introduced by Pierre-Charles Le Monnier in 1743 in the book La Théorie des Comètes. He aimed to resemble an Indigenous constellation of the Sami people in Northern Scandinavia, where he had travelled to on a geodetic expedition.

names.name: Rasalas
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period ra's alasad (al-shamali), "(the Northern [Part] of) the Lion's Head." As originally applied, mu Leo was "Rasalasad Borealis" abbreviated in the first Western astronomical source as "Rasalas. Bor.," for lack of space in the line), and epsilon Leo was "Rasalasad Australis" (after the Arabic).

names.name: Rasalgethi
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from its name for the Arabic Almagest period ra's al-jathi, "the Kneeler's Head."

names.name: Rasalhague
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from its name for the Arabic Almagest period ra's al-hawwa', "the Head of the Serpent Collector."

names.name: Rasalnaqa
names.origin: The group of stars that Ptolemy called "The Hand of Andromeda" is also called "The Head of the She-Camel" in an Indigenous Arabian tradition. as-Sufi (11th c. CE) combines these two traditions, and so does IAU by naming one of the star after "the hand" and the other one "the camel's head"

names.name: Rastaban
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from the name for the Arabic Almagest period ra's al-tinnin, "the Serpent's Head," for gamma Dra. Transferred to beta Dra in recent times (originally Ptolemy had gamma Dra on the "head," and beta more specifically on the "eye").

names.name: Regulus
names.origin: The name is a Latin translation of the ancient Greek name for this star:, "the (little) King" or "the Kingly One", which is a translation of the Sumerian name of the star: LUGAL (The King). The Romans, following the Greeks, called the star stella regia, "the Royal Star". Later, the Medieval Latin Almagest, translating from the Arabic (where in one version the original Greek diminutive had been lost), had rex, "the King". The form "Regulus" (again, the [little] King") first appears in 1522, obviously formed by some Early Modern scholar after the Greek diminutive name.

names.name: Revati
names.origin: Revatī is a Hindu mother goddess, in Sanskrit written. It is also the name of the 27th nakshatra and specifically the star zeta Psc. The Sun passing this star designates the beginning of a new (solar) year.

names.name: Rhombus
names.origin: Lacaille named the constellation ''Réticule Rhomboïde'' which may refer to the earlier constellation "Rhombus" that Habrecht (1621) defined in the area.

names.name: Rigel
names.origin: From an abbrevation of its pre-Islamic Arabian (and Arabic) name rijl al-jauza', the Foot of al-jauza'." "Rigel" is one of the oldest Arabic star names applied in the West, from the end of the 10th century A.D.

names.name: Rigil Kentaurus
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its name for the Arabic Almagest period rijl qanturis, "the Centaur's Foot". Today the name is occasionally seen abbreviated as "Rigil Kent."

names.name: Rotanev
names.origin: Nicolaus Venator, responsible for 1814 star catalogue)

names.name: Ruchbah
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period rukbat dhat al-kursiy, "the Knee of the Lady of the Chair."

names.name: Rukbat
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of its name for the Arabic Almagest period rukbat al-rami, "the Archer's Knee".

names.name: Sabik
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its pre-Islamic Arabian name al-sabiq, of uncertain meaning or connection. The name might mean literally "the Preceding One" or "the One Arriving First in a Race". Other sources give the name in the dualis form (for the two stars zeta and eta Oph), and in the plural form (for more than two stars).

names.name: Saclateni
names.origin: Eta and Zeta Aurigae, the 8th and 9th stars of Auriga in the Almagest, were referred to as "the kids" - Eriphoi (Greek), Haedi (Latin), al-Jadayain (Arabic; al-Sufi). Hyginus (Poetica Astronomica, 2. 13) mentions the Greek astronomer Cleostratus of Tenedos (5th cen. BC) pointed out "the kids" among the stars. "Saclateni" appeared in the Alfonsine Tables ("Tabule astronomice Alfonsi Regis", 1492 print) and may be a corrupted Latinization of the Arabic Gadi-thani, "second kid" (Mesnard 1949, "Les noms arabes d'étoiles", Ciel et Terre, Vol. 65, p. 70)

names.name: Sadachbia
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic lunar mansion name sa(d al-akhbiya, for gamma, pi, zeta and eta Aqr. A possible meaning for the name is "the Lucky (Stars) of the Tents", but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Sadalbari
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the pre-Islamic Arabian name sa'd al-bari', for lambda and mu Peg. A possible meaning for the name is "the Lucky (Stars) of the Excelling One," but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Sadalmelik
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic name sa(d al-malik, for alpha and omicron Aqr. A possible meaning for the name is "the Lucky (Stars) of the King", but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Sadalsuud
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic lunar mansion name sa(d al-su(ud, for beta and xi Aqr, and 46 Cap. A possible meaning for the name is "the Luckiest of the Lucky (Stars)", but the exact historical connections are unknown.

names.name: Sadr
names.origin: "Breast" in Arabic

names.name: Safina
names.origin: an Indigenous Arabic constellation of the Ship was between Diphda and Fomalhaut (see al Qutayba); WGSN picked one of the possible stars in the area. considering the close vicinity of the Greek star name "Hydor" (The Water) north of it, it becomes a sunken treasure ship.

names.name: Saiph
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the Arabic asterism name saif al-jabbar, the Giant's Sword," for eta, c, theta, and iota Ori. Wrongly applied as a star name to kappa Ori in recent times.

names.name: Salm
names.origin: Bayer (1603) mentions three names: Markab, Sagma and its corruption Salma. Allen (1899, 329) considers the correct form "Salm", a Leathern Bucket.

names.name: Sargas
names.origin: MUL.SHAR.GAZ, "mul" is the Sumerian designator for stars and constellations, "Shargaz" and "Sharur" are two weapons of Marduk (the city god of Babylon and highest god of the Babylonian pantheon after 1250 BCE). The line I ii 31-32 in MUL.APIN read: "Two stars which stand in the sting of the Scorpion: Sharur and Shargaz", so these star names have originally been given to the stars lambda and upsilon Sco. The Mesopotamian name "Sargas" was linked to the star Theta Sco by Robert Brown Jr. (1893; "Euphratean Stellar Researches Part II.") and its subsequent mention in R. H. Allen's (1899) "Star-names and Their Meanings" popularized its subsequent use.

names.name: Sarin
names.origin: Name of unknown etymology from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965). It is probably a part of the body. The word probably is not of Semit's origin,

names.name: Sarvvis
names.origin: Sarvvis, the reindeer or moose (bull), is an Indigenous constellation, used by the Sami people of northern Scandinavia.

names.name: Sceptrum
names.origin: from the obsolete constellation of Sceptrum Brandenburgicum

names.name: Scheat
names.origin: From the Arabic word al-saq, "the shin," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing delta Aqr. Wrongly transferred as a star name to beta Peg in late medieval times.

names.name: Schedar
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from the Arabic word al-sadr, "the breast," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star.

names.name: Secunda Hyadum
names.origin: The Latin term Hyadum II goes back to Flamsteed (1729) in analogy to Hyadum I or Prima Hyadum

names.name: Segin
names.origin: Name of unknown etymology from the "Atlas Coeli Skalnaté Pleso" of Czech astronomer Antonín Bečvář (1901-1965).

names.name: Seginus
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the Greek constellation name (Boötes), which was transliterated and then corrupted in the manuscripts of the Arabic Almagest. One of these corruptions, in turn, was transliterated into Latin as theguius, which became further corrupted into cheguius, ceginus, etc. One form, Ceginus, was applied as a star name by late medieval times, and "Seginus" is its recent spelling.

names.name: Shakata
names.origin: Rohinīśakata is the Cart of Rohini, a deity represented in the star Aldebaran, and one of the nakshatras. Her cart is traditionally seen in the Hyades star cluster; WGSN represents it by a star within their central area to honour the area's cultural importance.

names.name: Shakh
names.origin: ŠAH, Pig, is a Sumerian constellation attested in MUL.APIN (dating between 1350 and 1150 BCE). The two stars Alpha and Beta Sagittae look like the nose of the Mesopotamian constellation The Pig. WGSN applies the name to Beta.

names.name: Sham
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name al-sahm, "the Arrow," for Sagitta.

names.name: Shangcheng
names.origin: Shàng Chéng (The Great Imperial Minister) and Shào Chéng (The Second Imperial Minister) are the two stars located to the left and right of the northern gate of the Zi Gong (Purple Palace) / Ziwēi Yuán (Purple Enclosure).

names.name: Shangwei
names.origin: Shàng Wèi (The Great Imperial Guard) is the name of the fifth star on the right wall and the sixth star on the left wall of the Zi Gong (Purple Palace) / Ziwēi Yuán (Purple Forbidden Enclosure), counting northward from the southern gate. Its corresponding star has changed many times throughout history.

names.name: Shaomin
names.origin: Taimin (or Damin) for o Leo and Shaomin (rho Leo) are the two southernmost stars of the Xuanyuan constellation. They were used to star names in ancient China.

names.name: Shaowei
names.origin: Shào Wèi (The Second Imperial Guard) is the sixth star on the right wall of the Zi Gong (Purple Palace) or Ziwēi Yuán (Purple Forbidden Enclosure), counting northward from the southern gate. Although its identification has varied across historical sources, all recorded versions consistently place it within the modern constellation Camelopardalis.

names.name: Shatabhisha
names.origin: Śatabhisa, literally "hundred physicians", is the name of the 24th nakshatra of Vedic astronomy. Its earliest attestation is in a Vedic religious text (Atharvaveda) from the first millennium BCE, and an astronomy text (Vedanga Jyotisha) that dates around 300 BCE. As the yogatara (main star) of this nakshatra, lambda Aquarii stands "pars pro toto" for the entire constellation.

names.name: Shaula
names.origin: The Arabic lunar mansion "Al Shaula" ("the sting") refers to the pair Lambda and Upsilon Sco (Al Sufi), the two stars that have been called "the sting of the Scorpion" even in MUL.APIN (I ii 31-32) but with different proper names there. "Shaula" appeared more in early modern literature for the pair of stinger stars after Hyde's (1665) translation of Ulugh Beg, and specifically for Lambda Sco after Piazzi's (1814) Palermo Catalog.

names.name: Sheliak
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name al-salbaq, "the Harp," for Lyra. salbaq was a Greek loanword in Arabia, and was one of three names of musical instruments used by the Arabics for Lyra. Still other names were alsulalfat, and al-lura.

names.name: Shengong
names.origin: Shengong (Divine Palace) is a subsidiary asterism attached to the lodge Wěi, Tail [of the Azure Dragon], located to the left of its determinative star and consisting of only one star (single star-asterism).

names.name: Sheratan
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic lunar mansion name al-shara-tan, for beta and gamma Ari. The name means "two" of something, but the complete meaning is uncertain. Some Arabic authors suggested that it meant "the Two Signs", implying these stars as some kind of celestial indicator; others assumed it meant "the Two Horns", referring to the Arabic figure of al-hamals here.

names.name: Shimu
names.origin: "Tian Shi Mu", The Eye of the Celestial Pig, is the oldest preserved name for this star in China. Later, this region was named Kui, the Legs, and zeta And was (in historical times before Qing Dynasty) used as the determinative star of this constellation and lunar mansion.

names.name: Simmakh
names.origin: Unlike most zodiac constellations, Pisces was not an ancient Mesopotamian constellation. Cuneiform literature calls this area SIM.MAH, The Swallow. WGSN picked a star that is inside its constellation area, despite transformations, at all times between 1400 and 100 BCE.

names.name: Sirius
names.origin: From its ancient Greek name, "the Scorching one", or "Brilliant One", appropriate for this brightest of the fixed stars. Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Situla
names.origin: A Latin word meaning "pot" or "bucket", used in Early Modern philological studies as the translation of the Arabic constellation name al-dalw, for Aquarius. Subsequently the word was applied as a star name to k Aqr. The Arabs located al-dalw ("the Well Bucket") in today's Square of Pegasus. In that location it corresponded to what in other cultures was Aquarius among the zodiacal signs. The Arabs subsequently used the indigenous name al-dalw for the Greek Water Pourer (Aquarius).

names.name: Skat
names.origin: Applied with various spellings since medieval times, from the Arabic word al-saq, "the shin", used in the Arabic Almagest in describing this star.

names.name: Solitaire
names.origin: extinct constellations invented by Le Monnier (1776), Latinized "Turdus Solitarius", was originally meant to remember the extinct bird "Rodrigues Solitaire", but always depicted as a Blue Rock Thrush.

names.name: Spica
names.origin: Its ancient Roman name meaning "the Ear of Grain", after the star's Greek name of identical meaning (in turn having obvious origins among the Babylonians and Sumerians). Reapplied in Early Modern times.

names.name: Stellio
names.origin: Hevelius, who invented the constellation Lacerta sive Stellio (modern Lacerta), gave it the alternative name Stellio in his star catalogue and atlas.

names.name: Stephanos
names.origin: , The Wreath, is the ancient Greek name of CrB. It can represent either the laurel wreath of an emperor or victorious athlete, or a bridal wreath.

names.name: Sualocin
names.origin: reversed Latin Nicolaus Venator, responsible for 1814 star catalogue)

names.name: Subra
names.origin: From the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion name al-zubra, "the Mane, or Shoulder," for delta and theta Leo, associated with the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism al-asad (see epsilon Gem; al-zubra was an alternative name for al-kharatan given under theta Leo). "Subra" was wrongly applied as a star name too Leo in recent times.

names.name: Suhail
names.origin: Applied in recent times and representing an abbreviation of any of several composite pre-Islamic Arabian names (for example suhail al-wazn, suhail al-muhlif) that Arabic authors variously attributed to brighter stars in the region of suhail. A Vel was among these brighter stars. Some of the composite names may have been authentic pre-Islamic Arabian names for far-southern stars, with their true identities unknown to the more northern Arabs, while others of them were surely the creations of pre-Islamic Arabian poets.

names.name: Sukhurmashu
names.origin: Sukhurmashu is the Akkadian original name for this goat-fish; it was considered a benevolent and philanthropic daemon that helps humans to stay healthy and vivid.

names.name: Sulafat
names.origin: Applied in recent times from the Arabic constellation name al-sulabfat, "the Tortoise," for Lyra, corresponding to the Greek image of a tortoise shell for the Lyre's soundboard.

names.name: Syrma
names.origin: From the Greek word μ, "train of a dress", used by Ptolemy in the Almagest in describing this star. The word was applied as a star name in recent times.

names.name: Tabit
names.origin: Arabic al-thābit 'the endurer (the fixed/constant one)'

names.name: Taiyangshou
names.origin: traditional Chinese single star asterism: Taiyangshou means "The Guardian of the Great Yang" and is the general in charge of the yang valve, symbolising Chief Minister. Xu, Pankenier and Jiang (2000) and Sun Shuwei (Stellarium) evaluating the medieval Song map, both identify chi UMa but Sun and Kistemaker (1997) studying the Han dynasty identify psi UMa.

names.name: Taiyi
names.origin: single star asterism: August Unity, Supreme One

names.name: Talitha
names.origin: Applied in recent times from an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name alqafza al-thalitha, "the Third Leap," for iota and kappa UMa. This pair, with the pairs lambda/mu and v/xi UMa, composed the pre-Islamic Arabian asterism qafazat al-ziba', "the Leaps of the Gazelles," imagined as the tracks left by those animals. In some later tradition, qafazat al-ziba' and adjacent asterisms were associated in a fable, where several gazelles leaped away from the Lion into a pond, leaving their tracks behind.

names.name: Tania Australis
names.origin: Applied in recent times from their pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qafza al-thaniya, "the Second Leap", and the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern," respectively.

names.name: Tania Borealis
names.origin: Applied in recent times from their pre-Islamic Arabian name al-qafza al-thaniya, "the Second Leap", and the Latin distinctions of "northern" and "southern," respectively.

names.name: Tarandus
names.origin: Tarandus is an alternative name for the Early Modern European constellation "Rangifer", the Reindeer, from Greek (reindeer), Latinised by Carl Linnaeus 1758 "Cervus Tarandus" for a species, Jamieson 1822 used "Rangifer tarandus" for the reindeer in the sky.

names.name: Tarazed
names.origin: Applied in recent times (with a misreading) from abbreviating the Persian asterism name shanin-i tarazu, "the Scale Beam", for alpha, beta and gamma Aql. The Persian name, in turn, was a medieval translation of these stars' Arabic name al-mizan, "the Balance".

names.name: Tarf
names.origin: Arabic:, Al-Tarf (The eyes of the lion) is one of the traditional "Lunar Stations". It is composed of the 2 stars: epsilon Leo and omicron Leo. However, the name has been in common use for beta Cnc as it was published in the Yale Bright Star Catalogue.

names.name: Taygeta
names.origin: These names were individually applied in Early Modern times from a family of characters in Greek mythology: Atlas, Pleione and their seven daughters, the Pleiades.

names.name: Tegmine
names.origin: A Latin word in the ablative case meaning "covering" or "shell" (nominative case would be "tegmen"), used in a Early Modern discussion of the constellation Cancer. The word was subsequently applied as a star name to zeta Cnc.

names.name: Tejat
names.origin: From the Arabic word tihyat, said to be the singular form of al-tahayi, an pre-Islamic Arabian name of unknown meaning and disputed identification. In some sources, the plural al-tahayi is assigned to eta, mu, and v Gem. As originally applied in recent times, eta was "Tejat Prior," and mu was Tejat Posterior."

names.name: Telum
names.origin: Telum, the Dart, has been used as an alternative name for Sagitta in European literature of the past millennium (e.g. Dürer 1515, Uranometria 1603, Kepler 1627). WGSN applies the name to the brightest star of the asterism.

names.name: Tengshe
names.origin: Tengshe or (Téng Shé, Flying Serpent) is a constellation created by ancient Chinese astrologers, dating back to the 2nd century BCE.

names.name: Tepennekhet
names.origin: Head of the Giant, the Giant (Nekhet) being an important Egyptian constellation, is a star name from the Ramesside Star Clocks (1400 and 1200 BCE).

names.name: Tepiamenit
names.origin: Menit, The Mooring Post, is an Egyptian constellation, preserved in Ramesside Star Clocks of the 2nd millennium BCE. Tepiamenit is the "Predecessor of the Pole" inside Menit.

names.name: Terebellum
names.origin: Ptolemy's Almagest lists four stars in a quadrilateral with omega Sgr the first in the list (the others being A, b, c Sgr). Bayer (1603) concludes this list with the note after "c": Has quatuor multi Terebellum seu π vocant. A "terebellum" is an auger, so it designates the asterism at the tip of the tail and originally not a specific star.

names.name: Theemin
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with one of the words used by Ptolemy to describe this star in the Almagest: μπ, "the bend [of the river]". This was misread by the Arabs, who transliterated the word as bhmn. This, in turn, was transliterated as beemun in the Medieval Latin Almagest, which was corrupted to beemin, beemim, etc. Then in Early Modern times, the derivation of the form beemim was erroneously attributed to the Hebrew word te'omim, "twins." Subsequently this erroneous word, written as Theemim, then "Theemin," was applied as a star name to any of the various dim stars running from u1 to h Eri.

names.name: Thuban
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the name for the Arabic Almagest period for gamma Dra: ra's al-tinnin, "the Serpent's Head." In medieval times this was transliterated into Latin as raztaben, rahtaben, razcaben, and several other corruptions (eventually leading to the name for beta Dra). By Early Modern times the form Rastaben had appeared, and this name was erroneously attributed, in its last part, to the Arabic word thu'ban, "serpent", rather than to al-tinnin (subsequently thu<ban was wrongly regarded as a name for the Arabic Almagest period for the constellation Draco). Finally in recent times, the erroneous word, written as "Thuban," was applied as a star name to alpha Dra.

names.name: Tiaki
names.origin: Makemson (1941: 261 #659) lists Tiaki as the Tuamotuan name for beta Gru, sourcing this to unpublished field data supplied by Kenneth P. Emory (ibid.: 197). However, Emory's star information does not appear in his later publications and has not been located to date in archives of his unpublished material. Stimson's Tuamotuan dictionary (1964: 526) gives the meaning of Tīaki as "guardian", "keeper" or "watchman", but does not list it as a star. He does, however, list Tīakitau as the name of an unidentified star on Anaa, which Makemson (1941: 261 #660) lists separately.

names.name: Tianbang
names.origin: Tiān Bàng (Celestial Flail) is a defensive weapon, attested as constellation since 100 BCE. WGSN represents it by its determinative star.

names.name: Tianbian
names.origin: Tiān Biàn (Market Officer) is a traditional Chinese asterism close to the Celestial Market super-constellation. It literally means “Celestial Cap" and describes a ceremonial headgear. The name is attested since around 100 BCE. WGSN represents it by its determinative star.

names.name: Tianfu
names.origin: Tianfu was an ancient Chinese constellation consisting of four stars. Their counting order has changed over time but we decided to take the name for the 1st star of the early (before Tang dynasty) version.

names.name: Tiangang
names.origin: Tiān Gāng (Celestial Rope) is a traditional Chinese constellation that represents large ropes used to pitch tents — and symbolically represents the Celestial Military Tent of the emperor on campaign.

names.name: Tianguan
names.origin: Chinese single star asterism, a celestial pass along the ecliptic which opens and closes

names.name: Tianji
names.origin: Celestial Discipline, is an ancient Chinese asterism of nine stars first recorded in the Western Han Shishi xingjing (Master Shi’s Star Canon).

names.name: Tianjinnan
names.origin: “Southern star of Tianjin”, the Celestial Ferry, is in the Chinese constellation that allows is celebrated to allow the celestial couple of The Girl and The Cowherd to meet once a year.

names.name: Tiansi
names.origin: Tiān Sì (Heavenly Quadriga) is an old Chinese asterism, attested for at least 2000 years. It comprises four of the five stars forming the constellation Wangliang and represents the four horses pulling the chariot. It may thus be regarded as a constituent sub-constellation/asterism of Wangliang. In the literature in English, the name "Ce" (old spelling: Tsih) can be found; WGSN corrects this misapplication of an old star name.

names.name: Tianyi
names.origin: Chinese single star asterism: heavenly unity

names.name: Tianyue
names.origin: Tiān Yuè (Celestial Keyhole) is a Chinese constellation believed to govern the functions of opening and closing.

names.name: Titawin
names.origin: Titawin (also known as Medina of Tetouan) is a settlement in northern Morocco and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Historically it was an important point of contact between two civilizations (Spanish and Arab) and two continents (Europe and Africa) after the 8th century.

names.name: Toliman
names.origin: Applied in recent times from some pre-Islamic Arabian name al-zulman, "the Ostriches." Stars in today's Centaurus were variously identified with one or more ostriches by the pre-Islamic Arabians, but what star or stars were originally designated is unknown.

names.name: Tonatiuh
names.origin: Tonatiuh was the Aztec god of the Sun.

names.name: Tonglingxing
names.origin: Tóng Líng (Phoenix Tree Mound) is a traditional Chinese star name at the right wall of the Purple Palace constellation, rarely used, but ~2000 years old. WGSN uses "Tonglingxing" to avoid confusion with an asteroid name.

names.name: Torcular
names.origin: The traditional name Torcularis septentrionalis (northern wine press) was taken from the 1515 Almagest (Latin translation) and abbreviated.

names.name: Triminus
names.origin: The star iota Tri (iota or 6 Trianguli) is the brightest one in the early modern variant of a lesser triangle next to the recognisable classical asterism within the constellation Triangulum. The name is composed of the IAU-abbreviation "Tri" and Hevelius's name "Minus" for the lesser triangle. The name applies to the visible dot in the sky, so that "iot Tri A" is "Triminus A". The other component is not visible to the naked eye.

names.name: Tugongli
names.origin: Tu Gong Lì (Clerks of the Earth Official) is an ancient Chinese two-star asterism.

names.name: Tureis
names.origin: From the Arabic word al-turais, "the Little Shield," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing several stars (rho Pup not among them) in the constellation Argo. Wrongly applied as a star name to rho Pup in recent times.

names.name: Tusizuo
names.origin: Tú Sì ("Butcher's Shop") is a Chinese asterism consisting of two stars, established by the Wuxian school during the Han dynasty. As "Tusi" could be confused with other celestial bodies named Tusi after two Persian astronomers (asteroid (10269) Tusi and asteroid (7058) Al-Tusi), WGSN chose to add a determinative here. The chosen star 95 Her is "the left one in Tusi", in Chinese "Tusizuo", so WGSN adopts this name.

names.name: Udang
names.origin: Udang, "the Shrimp", is an Oceanic name from Bali (Indonesia). It is anchored in the cultural calendar called "Palelintangan" which is attested for ~1300 years. Particularly whiteleg and tiger shrimp are leading fishery commodity in Bali with significant economic potential.

names.name: Udkadua
names.origin: The Sumerian term UD.KA.DU8.A is a compound, literally meaning "the storm demon with the gaping mouth". This Babylonian constellation is at least 3000 years old; the star named after it is its heel. It was highly important, as it was used for time-measurement for at least a millennium (if not longer).

names.name: Ukdah
names.origin: Kazwini knew the stars tau1, tau2 Hya as uqdah (or ukdah), Arabic "knot". Rhoads (1971) considers this asterism consisting of four stars: tau1, tau2, 33 and iota Hya.

names.name: Unukalhai
names.origin: Applied in recent times from its name for the Arabic Almagest period 'unuq al-hayya, "the Serpent's Neck."

names.name: Uridim
names.origin: The constellation of Lupus is one of the few ancient "Greek" constellation outside the zodiac that was directly taken over from a Babylonian constellation. The Sumerian term for this creature was UR.IDIM, later alternatively written "Uridimmu" in the Akkadian language (the literal Akkadian translation of UR.IDIM would be "kalbu šegû", according to lexical lists).

names.name: Urquchillay
names.origin: Urquchillay, the Llama of Many Colors, is the name of the Inka god of livestock and wildlife; it was the protector of animal. Its constellation covers large areas of Lyra; WGSN adopts the name for a star close the the god's heart.

names.name: Vega
names.origin: Applied in medieval times from an abbreviation of its pre-Islamic Arabian name alnasr al-waqi', "the Swooping Eagle (or Vulture)," alternatively used as an asterism name for alpha, epsilon, and zeta Lyr. "Vega" is one of the oldest Arabic star names applied in the West, from the end of the 10th century A.D.

names.name: Veritate
names.origin: From the latin "Veritas", truth. The ablative form means "where there is truth".

names.name: Vindemiatrix
names.origin: The formation of this name begins with the classical Greek name for this star: Protrygeter ("the Grape Gatherer") as it is given in the Almagest: omicron v μ. The Romans translated this name as vindemiator and other similiar masculine forms. Similarly, after a somewhat erroneous translation of the Greek name by the Arabs, the Medieval Latin translation in the Almagest was precedens vindemiatorem, "the One preceding the Grape Gatherer", modified in some editions of the Alphonsine Tables into precedens vindemitorem. The exact origin of the current, feminine "Vindemiatrix" from any of these forms is uncertain, but it first appeared in Early Modern times.

names.name: Waiping
names.origin: Wài Píng (Outer Fence) is a traditional Chinese asterism belonging to the Kui mansion, whose name-giving constellation was called a pig (Shimu) in ancient times. The fence makes the pigsty unseen.

names.name: Wasat
names.origin: From the Arabic word wasat, "middle," used by a Arabic commentator who was speculating on the meaning of the pre-Islamic Arabian constellation name al-jauza'. Reference was made to al-jauza's being in the "middle" (wasat) of the sky (perhaps meaning the celestial equator). The reference was intended to apply to the pre-Islamic Arabian figure located in today's Orion, however it was under the constellation which is today Gemini that the reference appeared (note the confusion between Orion and Gemini mentioned under alpha Ori). Therefore, after transliteration into Latin, it was in Gemini (to delta) that the word "Wasat" was arbitrarily applied as a star name in recent times.

names.name: Wazn
names.origin: Applied in recent times from some pre-Islamic Arabian name al-wazn, of unknown significance.

names.name: Wezen
names.origin: From the Arabic name al-wazn, for one of a pair of stars, the other one being hadari. Arabic authors ventured to identify these stars as alpha/beta Cen or alpha/beta Col, but exactly what two stars were originally intended, and the significance of their names, is unknown. As a common noun in Arabic, al-wazn means "the weight". "Wezen" was arbitrarily applied to delta CMa in recent times.

names.name: Wurren
names.origin: Wurren is the Wardaman name of zeta Phe, from the Northern Territory, Australia. Wurren means “child” and refers to the “Little Fish”, a child of Dungdung – the life-creating Frog Lady. Wurren gives water to Gawalyan, the echidna (Achernar), which they direct Earthly initiates to carry in small bowls. The water came from a great waterfall used to cool the people during the ceremony. Just as the water at the base of the waterfall keeps people cool and rises to the sky as mist, the water in the initiates’ bowls keeps them cool and symbolically transforms into clouds that bring the wet rains of the monsoon season. These ceremonies occur in late December when the weather is hot and these stars are high in the evening sky, signalling the start of the monsoon.

names.name: Xami
names.origin: The South African asterism "Eyes of the Lion" refers to alpha and beta Centauri. Assuming these bright stars are the eyes, the face of this creature "Xami" covers alf Cir, and the constellation Circinus does not have any mythology or alternative name. Therefore, WGSN decided for an Indigenous name for this main star of a constellation.

names.name: Xamidimura
names.origin: Originally spelled as three word "xami di mura" means "eyes of the beast" in the Khoekhoe language (South Africa). The term designates two stars which is why it was suggested (Hahn 1881) to refer to mu Sco as this star appears as a visual pair of two dots of light. Yet, today's identification popularized by the SAAO differs.

names.name: Xihe
names.origin: Xihe is the goddess of the sun in the Chinese mythology and also represents the earliest astronomers and developers of calendars in ancient China.

names.name: Xuange
names.origin: single star asterism: a halberd, the celestial lance or north lance.

names.name: Yaqana
names.origin: Yaqana is a mother llama and forms a super-constellation with Uñallamacha, the baby llama. They rise in the sky when baby llamas are born on Earth.

names.name: Yed Posterior
names.origin: Originally from the Arabic word al-yad, "the hand," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing these stars. yed was applied as a star name to delta Oph in medieval times. Then in recent times, this application was extended to include both delta and epsilon, with the addition of the Latin distinctions for "foremost" and "hindmost," respectively.

names.name: Yed Prior
names.origin: Originally from the Arabic word al-yad, "the hand," used in the Arabic Almagest in describing these stars. yed was applied as a star name to delta Oph in medieval times. Then in recent times, this application was extended to include both delta and epsilon, with the addition of the Latin distinctions for "foremost" and "hindmost," respectively.

names.name: Yildun
names.origin: From the Turkish word yildiz, "star." In Early Modern times this common noun was erroneously said to be a Turkish name for the Pole Star (alpha UMi). Misspelled as "Yildun," the word was arbitrarily applied as a star name to delta UMi in recent times.

names.name: Yunyu
names.origin: Yún Yu (Cloud and Rain) is a four-star Chinese asterism which forms a super-constellation with Pili and Leidian; it is associated with plentiful, auspicious rainfall and the flourishing of plants. They have been documented for at least 2000 years.

names.name: Yunü
names.origin: Yunü is the star in the middle of the southernmost stars of the Xuanyuan constellation. The correct transliteration is "Yunü".

names.name: Yuyu
names.origin: Yuyu is a word from Javanese, inherited from Old Javanese "hayuyu", spoken on the island of Java, Indonesia. It means "freshwater crab". The animal can be found in rice fields in Indonesia and the constellation is attested for at least 1300 years.

names.name: Zaniah
names.origin: From an abbreviation of the pre-Islamic Arabian name zawiyat al-'awwa', "the Angle of al-'awwa'," for gamma Vir. Wrongly transferred to eta Vir in recent times.

names.name: Zaurak
names.origin: From the Arabic word zauraq, "boat," used in an unaginat1ve, nonclassical description of several stars near Eridanus (evidently the stars of today's Phoenix). Arbitrarily applied as a star name toy Eri in recent times.

names.name: Zavijava
names.origin: From a contraction of the pre-Islamic Arabian name zawiyat al-'awwa', "the Angle of al-'awwa'," for gamma Vir. Wrongly transferred to beta Vir in recent times. The stars beta, eta, gamma, and epsilon Vir marked the pre-Islamic Arabian lunar mansion al-'awwa' (with gamma in its "angle"), but the meaning of al-'awwa' is unknown.

names.name: Zhang
names.origin: determinitive star of lunar mansion Zhang (The Stomach [of the Red Fire Bird] or a Bow or Bird Catcher, an Extended Net, Spread or "to open") whose naming constellation constists of 6 stars according to sources back to the 3rd millennium BCE

names.name: Zhou
names.origin: This is a traditional Chinese star name of one of the stars in the historical Chinese constellation of Tianshi (Celestial Marketplace).

names.name: Zibal
names.origin: Applied in recent times from a misreading of the pre-Islamic Arabian name al-ri'al, "the Young of the Ostriches," for the numerous dim stars running between alpha Eri and alpha PsA (or, according to another tradition, those within the triangle formed by alpha Phe/alpha PsA/beta Cet).

names.name: Zibbatu
names.origin: Zibbatu is Akkadian for The Tails, referring to the "Tails of the Swallow", an asterism in the Mesopotamian constellation of The Swallow (SIM.MAH), which has been used in the Astronomical Diaries of Babylon for many centuries BCE to describe planet positions in Pisces.

names.name: Zosma
names.origin: From the Greek word μ, "girdle" or "loin cloth". In Early Modern times this word was erroneously said to have been used to describe delta Leo in a medieval Greek text. Correctly, the text has, "hip" or "lower back" (after Ptolemy). The name "Zosma" (transliterated from the erroneous Greek word) was applied in recent times.

names.name: Zubenelgenubi
names.origin: Applied in Early Modern times from its name for the Arabic Almagest period al-zubana al-janubi, the Southern Claw (of the Scorpion)." The stars of Libra were interpreted by the Baby!onians as "the Claws of Scorpius" (thus forming a much larger Scorpion), and alternatively (perhaps in a more recent stage) they were made an independent constellation, "the Balance." Both these conceptions lived on until the Greeks and, partly, the pre-Islamic Arabians. Previous to Greek influences, the pre-Islamic Arabians used the name al-zubanayan, "the Two Claws (of the Scorpion}," for the lunar mansion marked by alpha and beta Lib. (Ind-A al-zubanayan is obviously related etymologically to Babylonian zibanutu, but the latter, also marked by alpha and beta Lib, meant "the Balance"). Our modern name is occasionally seen abbreviated as Zuben'ubi".

names.name: Zubenelhakrabi
names.origin: Allen (1899) claims that this term was used for eta Lib while “properly belonging to gamma Scorpii”. He gives the name “Zubān al Akrab, the Scropion’s Claw,” with the spelling variants Zuban al Kravi, Zuben Acrabi, Zuben Hakrabi where the last one goes back to Bayer’s Uranometria (1603). Yet, Bayer’s gamma Scorpii is now sigma Lib (Brachium) and Bayer’s gamma Lib was named “in media lance Boreali prima et superior”.

names.name: Zubeneschamali
names.origin: Applied in Early Modern times from its name for the Arabic Almagest period al-zubana alshamali, "the Northern Claw (of the Scorpion)".

names.name: Zuoqi
names.origin: Zuo Qí (Left Flag) is a Chinese asterism consisting of nine stars and attested for more than 2000 years. It belongs to the super-constellation of flags and drums as signal transmitter. WGSN represents it by its determinative star.

names.name: Áldu
names.origin: Áldu, the Reindeer Cow, in Sami language. The Sami constellation of the reindeer is usually called with the male term "Sarvvis", but mythology reports it keeping its antlers during winter, which only females do.
